definition_zh: 小屋；门房；寄宿；租住；正式提出；卡住；嵌入
definition_en: a small house, especially at the gate of a park or estate; to stay in a place as a paying guest; to make a formal statement to an authority; to become fixed in one position
core_image: 山坡上一间矮小的木屋，夜里为过路的人留着一盏灯
scene: 山道尽头有一栋矮小的木屋，是守林人夜里落脚的地方。The keeper went back to his lodge before the snow closed the road.
sceneCN: 这里是「守林人居住的小屋」（第 1 个义项：山地或园林旁供人居住的小房子）；句意为在大雪封路之前，守林人回到了他的小屋。

pos.zh: 小屋；门房；（俱乐部的）分部
寄宿；租住；正式提出（申诉等）；卡住

derivatives.zh: 由 lodge 加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「房客；寄宿者」
由 lodge 加 -ing 构成，义为「寄宿处；临时住所」
由否定前缀 dis- 加 lodge 构成，义为「逐出；使离开原位」
由 lodge 加 -ment 构成，义为「存放；正式提交」

senses.title: A small house that gives shelter
senses.titleCN: 小屋；门房；园林中的居所
senses.definition: a small house, especially one at the gate of a park or estate, or one used for hunting and short stays
senses.definitionCN: 尤指公园或庄园门口的、或供狩猎和短期居住的小房子
senses.example: The gatekeeper lives in a stone lodge at the entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 守门人住在入口处一间石头门房里。
senses.why: Old French loge first meant an arbour or a leafy shelter, so the word names a modest building built to give cover rather than comfort.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 loge 最初指凉棚或用枝叶搭起的遮蔽处，所以这个词命名的是为遮风挡雨而建的简陋房子，不是讲究的住宅。

senses.title: To stay as a paying guest
senses.definition: to stay in someone else's house or in a rented room, usually paying for it
senses.definitionCN: 住在别人家里或租来的房间里，通常需要付费
senses.example: Two students lodged with a family near the campus.
senses.exampleCN: 两名学生寄宿在校园附近的一户人家里。
senses.why: The French verb logier meant to put someone under a roof, and English turned that shelter into an arrangement you pay for, so the noun grew a verb of living.
senses.whyCN: 法语动词 logier 意为把人安置到屋顶之下，英语把这层「安置」变成了付费的居住安排，名词于是长出「寄宿」的动词义。

senses.title: To make a formal statement to an authority
senses.definition: to submit a complaint, appeal or claim officially to a court, council or other authority
senses.definitionCN: 向法院、委员会或其他机构正式提交投诉、上诉或索赔
senses.example: The neighbours lodged a complaint about the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居们就噪音问题提出了投诉。
senses.why: The image shifts from a hut to a slot: a document is placed into the proper office the way a parcel is placed in a room, and it stays there as a record.
senses.whyCN: 意象从小屋转到「放入」：文件被放进相应的部门，就像包裹放进一间屋子，并且留在那里成为记录，这就是「正式提出」。

senses.title: To become fixed in one position
senses.definition: to become firmly stuck in a place, or to put something there so that it stays
senses.definitionCN: 牢牢卡在某个位置，或把某物放在那里不再移动
senses.example: A bullet lodged in the wall above the door.
senses.exampleCN: 一颗子弹嵌在门上方的那面墙里。
senses.why: The idea of finding a room extends to objects: whatever settles into a spot and cannot easily move has lodged there, as if it had taken shelter.
senses.whyCN: 「找到一间屋子」的想法延伸到物体：凡是落进某处、不容易再移动的东西，都算 lodged，仿佛它也在那里躲了起来。

intro.en: Lodge came into English from Old French, where a leafy arbour had already become a small building and a verb meaning to shelter someone.
intro.cn: lodge 经古法语进入英语；在法语里，用枝叶搭的凉棚已经变成小建筑，并且有了「安置、留宿」的动词用法。

items.en: Laubia or lobia named a covered gallery or arbour, probably borrowed from a Germanic word for a shelter of leaves.
items.cn: laubia 或 lobia 指带顶的回廊或凉棚，一般认为借自日耳曼语中表示「枝叶搭的遮蔽物」的词。

items.en: Loge meant a hut, arbour or small shelter, and it kept the picture of something built cheaply to give cover.
items.cn: loge 意为小屋、凉棚、简陋的遮蔽处，仍保留「临时搭建、只为遮风挡雨」的画面。

items.en: The verb logier meant to give someone lodging or to stay in a place, and it carried the word into English use.
items.cn: 动词 logier 意为给某人提供住处或自己住在某处，把这个词带入英语的日常使用。

items.en: Middle English lodgen covered both staying in a place and putting something down in a fixed spot.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lodgen 同时指「在某处住下」和「把东西放在固定位置」。

items.en: Modern English adds the legal sense of filing a complaint, and keeps lodger, lodging and dislodge in everyday use.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「正式提交投诉」这一法律义，并让 lodger、lodging、dislodge 留在日常用语里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same French shelter; the near-meaning group gathers other names for small buildings and for staying somewhere.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一个法语「遮蔽处」之上的词；近义组收其他表示小建筑和居住的词。

entries.definition: A person who pays to live in someone else's house.
entries.definitionCN: 付费住在别人房子里的人；房客。

entries.definition: A place to stay, often a rented room.

entries.definition: A place giving protection from weather or danger.
entries.definitionCN: 提供遮蔽、躲避风雨或危险的地方。

entries.definition: To live in a particular place.
entries.definitionCN: 居住在某处。

normalIntro.en: Lodge keeps one picture behind all its senses: something is given a place to stay, whether that is a person, a document or a bullet.
normalIntro.cn: lodge 的所有义项背后是同一个画面：一样东西被安置到一个能停留的位置，无论那是人、文件还是子弹。

normal.en: Lodge comes from Old French loge, a leafy arbour, so the first thing it names is a cheap shelter rather than a fine house.
normal.cn: lodge 来自古法语 loge，本指枝叶搭的凉棚，所以它最先命名的是简陋的遮蔽处，而不是好房子。

normal.en: Lodger adds -er to lodge: the person who lives in the little shelter and pays for it.
normal.cn: lodger 在 lodge 后加 -er：住进这间小屋并且付钱的人，就是房客。

normal.en: To lodge a complaint is to put the paper into the right office, the way a parcel is put into a room.
normal.cn: lodge a complaint 是把那份纸放进对应的部门，就像把包裹放进一间屋子。

normal.en: Dislodge takes dis-, meaning away, and drives the thing out of the spot it had settled in.
normal.cn: dislodge 用表示「离开」的 dis-，把已经安顿下来的东西赶出原来的位置。

normal.en: Loggia is a cousin from the same Latin gallery, and it still means a roofed open walkway.
normal.cn: loggia 是同出一个拉丁「回廊」词的亲戚，至今仍指带顶的开放走道。

abstract.en: A hut, a rented room and a bullet in a wall are the same sentence: something has found a place where it can stay.
abstract.cn: 小屋、租来的房间、嵌在墙里的子弹说的是同一句话：某样东西找到了可以停留的位置。

abstract.en: A complaint filed at a counter looks like a quiet act, but the paper stays in the building long after the person leaves.
abstract.cn: 在柜台递出的投诉看上去很安静，但人走了很久以后，那张纸还留在楼里。

abstract.en: The lamp in the gatehouse window is the warmest version of this word: shelter offered before anyone asks.
abstract.cn: 门房窗口那盏灯是这个词最温暖的版本：在有人开口之前就先给出一处遮蔽。

examples.en: A stray bullet lodged in the wall.
examples.cn: 一颗流弹嵌进了墙里。

examples.en: She lodged with a local family while studying abroad.
examples.cn: 她留学期间寄宿在当地一户人家。

examples.en: The residents lodged a complaint about the noise.
examples.cn: 居民们就噪音问题提出了投诉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「落居」——落脚居住的地方，就是小屋；住进去，便是寄宿。

root: 一般认为经古法语 loge（凉棚、小屋）进入英语，源头是晚期拉丁语 laubia 或 lobia（带顶的回廊），更早可追到日耳曼语表示「枝叶搭的遮蔽物」的词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a small shelter; from it come paying lodging, the legal act of placing a complaint, and anything that settles firmly in place.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是遮风挡雨的小屋；由此长出付费寄宿、把投诉正式放入案卷，以及任何牢牢停在原处的东西。

core.cn: 核心意象：天黑以后，一间矮木屋里亮着一盏为过路人留着的灯。

definition_en: a thick piece of cut or fallen tree; an official written record of events on a ship or aircraft; to write down events or figures in such a record; to travel or work a stated amount that is added to a total
core_image: 斧头落下去，树干断成一截一截，木纹里还渗着树脂
scene: 码头边的空地上，卡车后挡板放下，几截树干滚了下来。A thick log rolled off the truck and landed in the mud.
sceneCN: 这里是「伐下的整段树干」（第 1 个义项：未经加工的原木）；句意为一段粗大的原木从卡车上滚下来，落进了泥地里。

pos.zh: 原木；圆木；日志；记录簿
记录；把……记入日志；累计达到

由 log 加 -ing 构成，义为「伐木作业」
由 log 与 book 复合而成，义为「日志簿；记录本」

senses.title: A thick piece of cut tree
senses.definition: a thick piece of wood cut from a tree, or a whole trunk lying where it fell
senses.definitionCN: 从树上砍下的粗大木段，或倒在地上未经处理的整根树干
senses.example: The cabin walls were built from rough logs.
senses.exampleCN: 小木屋的墙是用粗糙的原木垒起来的。
senses.why: Middle English logge already meant a lump of wood, and this concrete sense has stayed at the centre of the word ever since.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语 logge 已经指一截木头，这个最具体的义项从中古一直留到今天，是整组词义的中心。

senses.title: An official record of a voyage or flight
senses.definition: an official written record of events kept on a ship, an aircraft or a machine
senses.definitionCN: 船、飞机或机器上保存的正式事件记录
senses.example: The captain wrote the storm into the ship's log.
senses.exampleCN: 船长把这场风暴写进了航海日志。
senses.why: Sailors measured speed by throwing a weighted piece of wood overboard and reading the line; the figures went into a book, and the book took the name of the wood.
senses.whyCN: 船员把一块系着重物的木头抛进海里测速，再读线上的刻度；数字记进本子，本子便沿用了那块木头的名字。

senses.title: To write something down in a record
senses.definition: to write an event, figure or message into an official record as it happens
senses.definitionCN: 把发生的事情、数字或消息在发生时写入正式记录
senses.example: Officers logged every radio message during the night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里，值班人员把每一条无线电消息都记了下来。
senses.why: Once log named the book, the same word could name the act of writing in it, so the record and the recording share one form.
senses.whyCN: 当 log 指那本簿子之后，同一个词自然也能指在簿子上书写这件事，于是「记录」和「被记录的内容」共用一个形式。

senses.title: To add up distance or working time
senses.definition: to travel or work an amount that is added to a running total
senses.definitionCN: 走过的距离或工作的时间被累加进一个总数
senses.example: The old bus has logged more than a million kilometres.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆旧巴士累计跑了一百多万公里。
senses.why: A logbook keeps a running total, so the verb came to mean reaching a figure that the book will hold.
senses.whyCN: 日志簿记的是一路累加的总数，所以动词又指达到某个会被写进簿子的数字。

intro.en: Log appears in Middle English as a word for a block of wood, and its further origin is uncertain; the record sense grew out of sailors measuring speed with a wooden chip.
intro.cn: log 在中古英语里就指一截木头，更早的来源不确定；记录义则从船员用木块测速这件事上长出来。

items.en: The word is first recorded in Middle English as logge, a block of wood, and no earlier form is securely attested.
items.cn: 这个词最早见于中古英语，写作 logge，指一截木头；更早的形式没有可靠的书面证据。

items.en: Logge named a cut block or a fallen trunk, the rough timber used for walls and for firewood.
items.cn: logge 指砍下的木块或倒下的树干，就是用来垒墙和烧火的粗木料。

items.en: Some dictionaries suggest a connection with Scandinavian words for something lying down, but the link is not certain.
items.cn: 一些词典认为它与斯堪的纳维亚语中表示「躺倒之物」的词有关，但这一联系并不确定。

items.en: A weighted wooden chip was thrown overboard to measure a ship's speed, and the readings were kept in a log book.
items.cn: 人们把一块加重的小木板抛到船外测速，读数记在航海日志里。

items.en: The word extends to any systematic record, then to computer sign-ins and to totals of distance or hours.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何系统化的记录，再进入计算机登录，也表示里程或工时的累计。

note.en: The look-alike group is built from log plus common English elements; the near-meaning group gathers words for wood and for written records.
note.cn: 形近组由 log 与常见英语成分组合而成；近义组收表示木材和书面记录的词。

entries.definition: An official book in which events are recorded.
entries.definitionCN: 记录事件的正式簿子；日志簿。

entries.definition: A person who cuts timber or keeps a record.
entries.definitionCN: 伐木的人，或负责记录的人。

entries.definition: The business of cutting trees for timber.
entries.definitionCN: 砍树取木材的行业；伐木。

entries.definition: Work that has piled up and is still waiting.

entries.definition: The act of signing into a computer system.
entries.definitionCN: 登录计算机系统的动作；登录。

entries.definition: Wood prepared for building, or standing trees.

entries.definition: A book in which a person writes about each day.
entries.definitionCN: 逐日写下经历的簿子；日记。

entries.definition: A written account of facts kept for the future.
entries.definitionCN: 为日后查阅而留下的事实记载。

normalIntro.en: Log starts as a plain word for a block of wood; the written record comes from the wooden chip sailors threw into the sea.
normalIntro.cn: log 起初只是「一截木头」的朴素说法；书面记录义则来自船员抛进海里的那块木片。

normal.en: Middle English wrote logge for a cut block of wood, and that solid sense never left the word.
normal.cn: 中古英语把砍下的一截木头写作 logge，这个实在的意思一直没有离开这个词。

normal.en: Sailors threw a weighted chip into the water, read the line, and wrote the figures in a book, so the book was named after the wood.
normal.cn: 船员把加重的小木片抛进水里，读线上的刻度，再把数字写进本子，本子便跟着木头得了名。

normal.en: Logger adds -er to log: the person who cuts the timber or keeps the record.
normal.cn: logger 在 log 后加 -er：砍木头的人，或负责记记录的人。

normal.en: Logbook is log and book joined directly, a book that holds the entries.
normal.cn: logbook 是 log 与 book 直接拼在一起，指收纳这些记录的本子。

normal.en: Backlog is back plus log: entries that piled up behind the rest, now any unfinished work.
normal.cn: backlog 是 back 加 log：堆在后面的记录，如今指任何积压未办的工作。

abstract.en: A cut block and a record book share one word, which suggests English treats a countable thing and a checkable trace as close neighbours.
abstract.cn: 一截木头和一本记录簿共用一个词，说明英语把「可数的东西」和「可查的痕迹」看得很近。

abstract.en: The chip thrown overboard is a reminder that a record is built from readings someone can check, not from memory.
abstract.cn: 抛到船外的那块木片提醒人：记录靠的是一次次可以核对的读数，而不是记忆。

abstract.en: Turn the pages of a log and time is cut into lines, which is the most practical picture this word offers.
abstract.cn: 一页页翻日志，时间就被切成一行一行，这是这个词最实用的画面。

examples.en: A fallen log blocked the path through the forest.
examples.cn: 一段倒下的原木挡住了穿过森林的小路。

examples.en: The pilot logged six hours of flying time that week.
examples.cn: 那名飞行员那一周累计飞行了六个小时。

examples.en: Every visitor is logged at the front desk.
examples.cn: 每位来访者都在前台做了登记。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「烙个」——把每天的事烙在本子上，就成了日志；log 既是木头，也是记录。

root: 来源不确定：中古英语 logge 已指「砍下的木块」，一般认为可能与斯堪的纳维亚语中表示「躺倒的树」的词有关，但没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The concrete sense is a cut trunk; the record sense grew from sailors writing down what a floating chip told them, and from there the word covers any systematic account.
sensesIntro.cn: 具体的义项是砍下的树干；记录义从船员把浮木读出的数字写下来开始，再扩展到任何系统化的记载。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an axe bites into a trunk and the cut block falls away.
core.cn: 核心意象：斧头咬进树干，砍下的一截木块滚落在地。

intro.en: The word is held together by a Middle English noun for a block of wood and a small set of English compounds and suffixes that build its family.

definition_zh: 逻辑；逻辑学；推理；条理；内在道理
definition_en: the study of valid reasoning; a system or process of reasoning; the sense or rationale behind something
core_image: 一排排前提像齿轮咬合，转动第一只，结论便被迫转到终点

senses.title: The discipline: the study of valid inference
senses.titleCN: 学科：研究有效推理的逻辑学
senses.definition: the branch of philosophy and science that studies the forms of valid reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 研究有效推理形式的哲学与科学分支
senses.example: She studied logic before turning to computer science.
senses.exampleCN: 她在转向计算机科学之前学过逻辑学。
senses.why: Greek logikē tekhnē was the 'art of reasoning', built on logos, 'word, reason, account'. The first sense is therefore the organized discipline that teaches how accounts must hang together.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 logikē tekhnē 是“推理之术”，建立在 logos“言词、理性、说明”之上。因此第一个义项就是教人如何让论述环环相扣的那门有组织的学科。

senses.title: The process: reasoning from premises
senses.definition: the process of drawing a conclusion from premises according to consistent rules
senses.definitionCN: 依照一致的规则从前提出发推出结论的过程
senses.example: The detective's logic led her to the only possible suspect.
senses.exampleCN: 侦探的推理把她引向唯一可能的嫌疑人。
senses.why: The discipline becomes an activity: a mind moves from what it accepts to what follows. The gears of the core image turn, and the conclusion is carried along whether one likes it or not.
senses.whyCN: 学科变成一种活动：心智从它接受的前提走向必然得出的结论。核心意象里的齿轮转动，结论不管人喜不喜欢都被带到终点。

senses.title: Sensible consistency: there is logic in it
senses.titleCN: 条理：事情说得通、前后一致
senses.definition: the quality of being sensible, consistent, or reasonable
senses.definitionCN: 明智、前后一致或合乎情理的性质
senses.example: There is a certain logic in her decision, even if I dislike it.
senses.exampleCN: 她的决定自有其道理，尽管我并不喜欢。
senses.why: When an account holds together, we say it has logic. The word moves from the formal rules to the everyday impression that nothing in the story contradicts anything else.
senses.whyCN: 当一个说法前后立得住，我们就说它有逻辑。这个词从形式规则转向日常印象：故事里没有任何一处与另一处相矛盾。

senses.title: Inner rationale: the logic of a situation
senses.titleCN: 内在道理：局势自身的运行逻辑
senses.definition: the underlying rationale that makes a situation, system, or institution work as it does
senses.definitionCN: 使某种局势、制度或体系如此运作的深层道理
senses.example: The logic of the market rewards speed over craftsmanship.
senses.exampleCN: 市场的逻辑奖励速度，而不是手艺。
senses.why: A system has its own forced sequence: given its rules, certain outcomes follow. Calling this its logic treats the system as an argument whose conclusion is already built in.
senses.whyCN: 一个体系有自己的强制序列：给定其规则，某些结果就会随之而来。把它称为“逻辑”，就是把该体系当作一个结论早已内置的论证。

senses.title: A formal system: Aristotelian, modal, fuzzy logic
senses.titleCN: 形式体系：亚里士多德逻辑、模态逻辑、模糊逻辑
senses.definition: a particular formal system of rules for valid inference, such as classical, modal, or fuzzy logic
senses.definitionCN: 某一套关于有效推理的形式规则体系，如经典逻辑、模态逻辑或模糊逻辑
senses.example: Modal logic adds rules for statements about necessity and possibility.
senses.exampleCN: 模态逻辑为关于必然性与可能性的陈述增加了规则。
senses.why: There is not one logic but many. Each system fixes its own symbols, axioms, and permitted moves, so 'a logic' names a game with explicit rules rather than reasoning in general.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑不止一套，而是有许多套。每个体系固定自己的符号、公理与允许的步骤，因此“一套逻辑”命名的是一场规则明确的游戏，而不是一般意义上的推理。

senses.title: Digital logic: gates and circuits
senses.titleCN: 数字逻辑：逻辑门与电路
senses.definition: the branch of electronics in which signals are combined by Boolean operations such as AND, OR, and NOT
senses.definitionCN: 电子学中用电平信号按与、或、非等布尔运算组合的分支
senses.example: The chip contains thousands of logic gates.
senses.exampleCN: 这块芯片包含数千个逻辑门。
senses.why: Formal rules become hardware: true and false turn into high and low voltage, and a gate output follows its inputs exactly as a conclusion follows premises. The abstract chain is now etched in silicon.
senses.whyCN: 形式规则变成硬件：真与假转为高电平与低电平，逻辑门的输出严格跟随输入，就像结论跟随前提。抽象的推理链此时被刻进硅片。

senses.title: Program logic: rules that decide behaviour
senses.titleCN: 程序逻辑：决定行为的规则
senses.definition: in computing, the set of rules in a program that determine how it responds to input
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域，程序中决定如何响应输入的一组规则
senses.example: The payment logic rejects cards with expired dates.
senses.exampleCN: 支付逻辑会拒绝过期日期的银行卡。
senses.why: Software encodes if-then structures: under condition A, do B. Business logic is the reasoning of an institution written as executable rules, so the same word covers both thought and machine.
senses.whyCN: 软件把“如果—那么”结构编码：在条件 A 下执行 B。业务逻辑就是把机构的推理写成可执行的规则，因此同一个词同时覆盖思维与机器。

senses.title: Argument structure: the chain from premise to conclusion
senses.titleCN: 论证结构：从前提到结论的链条
senses.definition: the structure of an argument, especially the relation between its premises and its conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 论证的结构，尤指前提与结论之间的关系
senses.example: The essay has a clear logic: each paragraph answers the objection raised before.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章逻辑清晰：每一段都回应前一段提出的反驳。
senses.why: Here logic is neither a discipline nor an inner rationale but the visible skeleton of a text. Each part must be held by the part before it, or the chain of proof breaks.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 logic 既不是学科，也不是内在道理，而是文本可见的骨架。每一部分都必须被前一部分扣住，否则证明链就断了。

senses.title: Usage boundary: countable only as a system
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：只有指“体系”时才可数
senses.definition: a usage limit: logic is usually uncountable; a logic or logics is used only for distinct formal systems, and logic is not a synonym for opinion or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 用法限制：logic 通常不可数；a logic 或 logics 只用于不同的形式体系，且 logic 不是 opinion 或 feeling 的同义词
senses.example: His anger is real, but it is not an argument in logic.
senses.exampleCN: 他的愤怒是真实的，但它在逻辑上不构成论据。
senses.why: The mass noun names reasoning as a substance, not a set of opinions. Counting begins only when separate rule-systems are compared. Emotion can motivate a claim, but it cannot supply the force of a conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 这个不可数名词把推理视作一种“质料”，而不是一堆观点。只有比较彼此独立的规则体系时才开始计数。情绪可以促使人提出主张，却不能提供结论的力量。

intro.en: Logic reaches English through Greek, Latin, and French. The chain logos to logikē to logica to logique is well documented; the Indo-European root *leg- is generally believed rather than certain.
intro.cn: logic 经由希腊语、拉丁语和法语进入英语。从 logos 到 logikē、logica、logique 的链条有清楚记载；其印欧词根 *leg- 只是一般认为，并非确定。

items.en: Greek logos meant 'word, speech, account, reason'. It could name a story told, an explanation given, or the rational order behind things.
items.cn: 希腊语 logos 意为“言词、言语、说明、理性”。它既可以指讲述的故事、给出的解释，也可以指事物背后的理性秩序。

items.en: Logos is generally traced to PIE *leg- 'to gather, pick up', specifically 'to pick words'. Speaking is pictured as gathering words and putting them in order; the deeper link is generally believed, not proved.
items.cn: logos 一般追溯到原始印欧语 *leg-“采集、拾起”，尤指“挑选词语”。说话被想象成把词语采集起来并排成次序；这一更深联系属于一般认为是，而非已经证明。

items.en: Logikē (tekhnē) meant the 'art of reasoning', the skill of using logoi well. Aristotle's works on argument turned that skill into a systematic study.
items.cn: logikē (tekhnē) 意为“推理之术”，即善用 logoi 的技能。亚里士多德关于论证的著作把这种技能变成了系统研究。

items.en: Latin logica and Old French logique carried the word westward. In the medieval curriculum logic was one of the three basic arts, alongside grammar and rhetoric.
items.cn: 拉丁语 logica 与古法语 logique 把这个词带到西方。在中世纪课程中，逻辑学与语法、修辞并列为三门基础技艺。

items.en: English logic appears in the 14c. Mathematical logic develops in the 19c., and digital logic in the 20c. gives the old art of reasoning a silicon body.
items.cn: 英语 logic 出现于 14 世纪。数理逻辑在 19 世纪发展起来，数字逻辑在 20 世纪给这门古老的推理之术装上了硅制的身体。

note.en: The first group shares the logos root or the log- shape; the second separates the discipline from reasoning, rationale, consistency, and one specific inference type.
note.cn: 第一组共享 logos 词根或 log- 词形；第二组把“逻辑学”与推理、根据、一致性以及一种具体推理类型分开。

entries.definition: following the rules of logic; sensible and consistent. It is the adjective built on logic.
entries.definitionCN: 符合逻辑规则的；有条理的。它是 logic 构成的形容词。

entries.definition: the organized movement and supply of goods and people. It comes from Greek logistikos 'skilled in calculating', also from logos.
entries.definitionCN: 货物与人员的有组织调运和供给。它来自希腊语 logistikos“擅长计算”，同样出自 logos。

entries.definition: a symbol or design used as a brand mark. It is shortened from logotype, from Greek logos 'word'.
entries.definitionCN: 用作品牌标记的符号或图案。它由 logotype 缩略而来，源自希腊语 logos“言词”。

entries.definition: the mental process of thinking things through. It is broader than logic and can include informal, practical thought.
entries.definitionCN: 把事情想通的思维过程。它比 logic 宽泛，可以包括非正式的、实践性的思考。

entries.definition: the reasons or explanation behind a decision or system. It names the content, not the formal study of inference.
entries.definitionCN: 某一决定或体系背后的理由或解释。它命名内容，而不是对推理的形式研究。

entries.definition: the property of parts fitting together without contradiction. It is one test of logic, not logic itself.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分彼此相容、不矛盾的性质。它是逻辑的一项检验，而不是逻辑本身。

entries.definition: inference from general premises to a necessary conclusion. It is one branch of logic, not the whole field.
entries.definitionCN: 从一般前提到必然结论的推理。它是逻辑学的一个分支，而不是整个领域。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: logos as word and reason, the real phrases formal logic and logic gate, and the everyday 'there is no logic in it'.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：作为言词与理性的 logos、真实短语 formal logic 与 logic gate，以及日常说法“毫无逻辑”。

normal.en: Logos meant 'word, account, reason'; logic is the art of making an account hold together.
normal.cn: logos 意为“言词、说明、理性”；logic 就是让一套说明站得住的技术。

normal.en: Formal logic writes the rules down: if the premises are true and the form is valid, the conclusion must be true.
normal.cn: formal logic 把规则写下来：如果前提为真且形式有效，结论必然为真。

normal.en: The logic of a situation is its inner forced sequence: given those rules, this outcome follows.
normal.cn: the logic of a situation 指局势内在的强制序列：给定那些规则，这个结果就会随之而来。

normal.en: A logic gate is the same reasoning in hardware: high and low inputs produce an output by rule.
normal.cn: 逻辑门是同一套推理的硬件版本：高、低输入按规则产生输出。

normal.en: Logical and illogical split the world into what follows and what contradicts itself.
normal.cn: logical 与 illogical 把世界分成两类：推得下去的，和自相矛盾的。

abstract.en: A chain of premises: each link is forced, and the last link cannot refuse the pull of the first.
abstract.cn: 一条前提链：每一环都是被迫的，最后一环无法拒绝第一环的拉力。

abstract.en: A transparent machine: put premises in at the top, and only the conclusion comes out at the bottom; emotion stays outside.
abstract.cn: 一台透明的机器：前提从上方放入，只有结论从下方出来；情绪留在机器之外。

abstract.en: A skeleton that holds an argument upright: remove one bone and the whole body of proof collapses.
abstract.cn: 一副撑起论证的骨架：抽掉一根骨头，整个证明的身体就塌了。

examples.en: The argument is elegant, but its logic is flawed at the second step.
examples.cn: 这个论证很漂亮，但它的逻辑在第二步就有漏洞。

examples.en: There is a simple logic to her method: test the cheapest fix first.
examples.cn: 她的方法有一个简单的内在道理：先试最便宜的修法。

examples.en: Modern processors are built from millions of logic gates.
examples.cn: 现代处理器由数百万个逻辑门构成。

dict_mnemonic.text: “老季克”——老季讲话条理清楚，句句都推得下去 → logic 逻辑

root: 希腊语 logos“言词、理性、说明”，经 logikē tekhnē“推理之术”而来；核心是“用有章法的言词把道理讲通”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of logic, all from logos as ordered speech: the discipline, the act of reasoning, the feel of consistency, the rationale inside a system, a formal rule-system, silicon gates, program rules, the skeleton of an argument, and the boundary of countable uses.
sensesIntro.cn: logic 的九个义项都出自 logos 作为“有秩序的言词”：学科、推理行为、前后一致的感觉、体系内的道理、形式规则体系、硅片上的门、程序规则、论证骨架，以及可数用法的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ordered words lock together and force a conclusion.
core.cn: 核心意象：有次序的言词彼此咬合，迫使结论出现。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE AND ITS SYSTEMS: logic is both the study of valid form and the named formal systems it compares.
branches.cn: 学科及其体系：logic 既是对有效形式的研究，也是它所比较的各套具名形式体系。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE SKELETON: reasoning moves from premise to conclusion, and the written argument shows that chain.
branches.cn: 行为与骨架：推理从前提到结论，书面论证则展示这条链。

branches.en: CONSISTENCY AND RATIONALE: an account holds together, and a system carries its own forced logic.
branches.cn: 一致性与内在道理：一套说明前后立得住，一个体系则带有自身强制的逻辑。

branches.en: MACHINES: Boolean gates and program rules turn inference into hardware and code.
branches.cn: 机器：布尔门与程序规则把推理变成硬件与代码。

branches.en: BOUNDARY: logic is mass-noun reasoning, countable only when separate systems are meant.
branches.cn: 边界：logic 是不可数的推理，只有指彼此独立的体系时才可数。

intro.en: Logic is a Greek-derived noun ending in -ic. English builds the adjective with -al, the adverb with -ally, the person with -ian, and the negative with il-.
intro.cn: logic 是源自希腊语、以 -ic 结尾的名词。英语用 -al 构成形容词，用 -ally 构成副词，用 -ian 构成人物名词，用 il- 构成否定。

latinIntro.en: The family rests on Greek logos 'word, reason'. Dialogue, monologue, logistics and analogy all contain that same second element or its derivative.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族建立在希腊语 logos“言词、理性”上。dialogue、monologue、logistics、analogy 都含有同一词素或其派生形式。

items.meaning: following the rules of logic; sensible
items.meaningCN: 逻辑的；合乎逻辑的（-al 表示“与……有关”）
items.example: That is the logical conclusion from the evidence.
items.exampleCN: 那是从证据得出的合乎逻辑的结论。

items.meaning: in a way that follows from the premises
items.meaningCN: 逻辑上；合乎逻辑地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Logically, the second claim depends on the first.
items.exampleCN: 从逻辑上说，第二个主张依赖于第一个。

items.meaning: a person who studies or works with logic
items.meaningCN: 逻辑学家（-ian 表示从事该学科的人）
items.example: The logician rewrote the proof in symbols.
items.exampleCN: 这位逻辑学家用符号重写了证明。

items.meaning: not following from the premises; inconsistent
items.meaningCN: 不合逻辑的；缺乏条理的（il- 表示否定）
items.example: It is illogical to expect a different result from the same input.
items.exampleCN: 指望同样的输入产生不同的结果是不合逻辑的。

items.example: The noun is the source of logic and of -logy.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是 logic 与 -logy 的来源。

items.example: The stem appears in dialogue, catalogue and logic.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 dialogue、catalogue 与 logic。

items.example: It shapes logical, the adjective built on logic.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 logical 这一形容词。

items.example: The ending marks logic as a discipline, logike in Greek.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把 logic 标为一门学问，希腊语作 logike。

items.meaning: a formal argument from two premises
items.example: The syllogism is the oldest tool of formal logic.
items.exampleCN: 三段论是形式逻辑最古老的工具。

latinEntries.meaning: a conversation between two or more people
latinEntries.meaningCN: 对话；对白（dia- 表示“之间”，logos 表示“言词”）

latinEntries.meaning: a long speech by one person
latinEntries.meaningCN: 独白；长篇独语（mono- 表示“单一”）

latinEntries.meaning: the organized supply and movement of goods and people
latinEntries.meaningCN: 物流；后勤（源自“擅长计算”，与 logos 同族）

latinEntries.meaning: a comparison based on a shared relation
latinEntries.meaningCN: 类比；类推（按相同的比例或关系作比较）

definition_zh: 合乎逻辑的；合理的；逻辑学的；条理清楚的
definition_en: following the rules of valid inference, or sensible and well ordered
core_image: 黑板上每一步都从上一行推出，写完最后一行时，结论已经无处可躲
scene: 数学教室的黑板上，老师把条件一行行写下去，最后一行还没落笔，后排已经有学生点头。The argument was logical at every step, so the conclusion seemed unavoidable.
sceneCN: 这里 logical 指「每一步都由前一步合法推出」（第 1 个义项：合乎有效推理）；句意为这个论证每一步都合乎逻辑，所以结论显得无法回避；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 合乎逻辑的；合理的；逻辑学的；有条理的

senses.title: Following valid inference
senses.definition: arranged so that each step is licensed by the rules of inference
senses.definitionCN: 安排得使每一步都由推理规则许可
senses.example: The argument was logical at every step, so the conclusion seemed unavoidable.
senses.exampleCN: 这个论证每一步都合乎逻辑，所以结论显得无法回避。
senses.why: The Greek root means 'word' and 'reason at work', so the adjective first says that the arrangement follows reason's rules.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根意为「言辞」与「运作中的理性」，因此这个形容词首先说明安排合乎理性的规则。

senses.title: Sensible and practical
senses.definition: being the choice or arrangement that a sensible person would make
senses.definitionCN: 是明理的人会作出的选择或安排
senses.example: Taking the earlier train was the logical thing to do.
senses.exampleCN: 坐早一班车才是合理的做法。
senses.why: Outside formal proof, valid inference is replaced by ordinary good judgment, and the word follows the looser use.
senses.whyCN: 在形式证明之外，有效推理被日常判断替代，这个词也随这种较松的用法走。

senses.title: Belonging to the discipline of logic
senses.definition: relating to logic as a formal subject of study
senses.definitionCN: 与作为正式研究科目的逻辑学相关
senses.example: A logical system needs rules for negation before it can do anything else.
senses.exampleCN: 一个逻辑系统先要有否定规则，才谈得上做别的。
senses.why: Once the discipline was named, its adjective began to describe the objects inside it.
senses.whyCN: 学科一旦被命名，它的形容词就开始描写学科内部的对象。

senses.title: Internally consistent
senses.definition: not contradicting itself, so that the parts can hold together
senses.definitionCN: 不自相矛盾，因此各部分能彼此撑住
senses.example: The account was logical but built on a false premise.
senses.exampleCN: 这套说法前后一致，却建立在一个假前提上。
senses.why: Consistency is the minimum that reasoning requires: no step may cancel an earlier one.
senses.whyCN: 自洽是推理的最低要求：任何一步都不能取消前面某一步。

senses.title: The expected next step
senses.definition: following so directly that it appears forced
senses.definitionCN: 接得如此直接，以致显得非如此不可
senses.example: Retirement was the logical end of a forty-year career.
senses.exampleCN: 退休是四十年职业生涯顺理成章的终点。
senses.why: When the chain is tight, the last link looks inevitable rather than chosen.
senses.whyCN: 当链条足够紧，最后一环看起来就不是选择，而是必然。

senses.title: Clear-headed as a person
senses.definition: describing a mind that proceeds in order and does not jump
senses.definitionCN: 形容心思按顺序推进、不跳跃
senses.example: She is a logical thinker even under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 即使在压力下，她也是思路清晰的思考者。
senses.why: The same quality that belongs to arguments is transferred to the people who make them.
senses.whyCN: 属于论证的性质被转移到制造论证的人身上。

senses.title: Of boolean operations in computing
senses.definition: in computing, describing operations on true and false values
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域，形容对真值与假值进行的运算
senses.example: A logical error is often a single reversed condition.
senses.exampleCN: 逻辑运算上的错误常常只是一个条件写反了。
senses.why: Machines were built on the formal rules of inference, so the discipline's adjective became a technical label.
senses.whyCN: 机器建立在形式推理规则之上，于是这门学科的形容词成了技术标签。

senses.title: Ordered and methodical
senses.definition: laid out in an order where each part has a place
senses.definitionCN: 按某种次序排列，使每一部分各就其位
senses.example: Arrange the files in a logical order before the audit.
senses.exampleCN: 审计之前把文件按条理排好。
senses.why: Order is the visible trace of reasoning, even when no conclusion is being drawn.
senses.whyCN: 即使没有在得出结论，条理也是推理留下的可见痕迹。

intro.en: Logical comes from a Greek word for 'of speech or reason', which reached English through Latin and French. Its root treats speaking and reasoning as one act.
intro.cn: logical 来自希腊语中意为「属于言辞或理性的」的词，经拉丁语与法语进入英语。它的词根把说话与推理当作同一件事。

items.en: Logos meant 'word, speech, account, reason'. The same noun served for a sentence, a story, a ratio and the order of the world.
items.cn: logos 意为「词、言语、说明、理性」。同一个名词既可指一句话、一个故事、一个比值，也可指世界的秩序。

items.en: The verb behind the noun meant 'to say, to pick out, to gather'. Speech and selection share one root because speaking was seen as selecting words.
items.cn: 名词背后的动词意为「说、挑出、收集」。说话与选择共享一个词根，因为说话被视为在挑选词语。

items.en: The adjective meant 'skilled in speech or reasoning', and it named the art of argument rather than a branch of study.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为「擅长言辞或推理的」，它指论证的艺术，而不是一门学科。

items.en: Latin borrowed the adjective and the noun; Old French passed them to English, where the noun first named the art of arguing well.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入该形容词与名词；古法语把它们传给英语，名词最初指善于论证的艺术。

items.en: As a taught subject, the noun settled into its modern sense, and the adjective came to describe whatever obeyed its rules.
items.cn: 作为被教授的科目，名词固定为现代意义，形容词则用来描写任何服从其规则的东西。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of the Greek verb is not established, and the reconstructed Indo-European root proposed for it is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个希腊动词的更早来源没有定论，为它提出的印欧词根属重构，只是假说。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same speech-and-reason root that are easy to confuse; the second holds near neighbours for being sensible or orderly.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「言辞与理性」词根、容易混淆的词；第二组是表示「明理」或「有条理」的近义词。

entries.definition: The discipline or the system of rules; the adjective describes what follows those rules.
entries.definitionCN: 指学科或规则体系；形容词则描写服从这些规则的东西。

entries.definition: From a Greek word for reckoning: it names the practical business of moving and supplying, not reasoning.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊语中指「计算」的词：指运输与补给的实际事务，而非推理。

entries.definition: One who studies the discipline, not something that conforms to it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究这门学科的人，而不是服从它的某物。

entries.definition: Built on the same noun with a prefix meaning 'according to': it names a comparison, not a rule of inference.
entries.definitionCN: 同一名词加意为「按照」的前缀：指比较，而非推理规则。

entries.definition: It adds a judgment about fairness or moderation, which logical does not contain.
entries.definitionCN: 多了对公平或适度的判断，而 logical 不含这一层。

entries.definition: It claims only that the parts do not clash, leaving open whether the whole is valid.
entries.definitionCN: 只声称各部分不冲突，至于整体是否有效则不论。

entries.definition: It praises a method followed throughout, even where the method itself is not logical.
entries.definitionCN: 称赞贯穿始终的方法，即使方法本身并不合乎逻辑。

entries.definition: In logic it means both correctly structured and built on true premises, a stronger claim than logical.
entries.definitionCN: 在逻辑中兼指结构正确与前提为真，比 logical 的主张更强。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Greek root means both 'word' and 'reason', so logical is about words that hold together by reason.
normal.cn: 希腊词根同时意为「言辞」与「理性」，所以 logical 说的是靠理性站得住的话。

normal.en: The family runs logic, logical, logically, logician, logicalness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 logic、logical、logically、logician、logicalness。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the chain: a logical step, a logical conclusion, a logical order.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出链条：合乎逻辑的一步、合乎逻辑的结论、逻辑顺序。

normal.en: The same root appears in words for dialogue, analogy and catalogue, all built on speech or gathering.
normal.cn: 同一个词根还出现在表示对话、类比与目录的词里，都由「说话」或「收集」构成。

normal.en: Computing uses the word for operations on true and false, because machines run on these rules.
normal.cn: 计算机领域用这个词指对真假的运算，因为机器就运行在这些规则上。

abstract.en: Picture a row of dominoes standing close enough that the first one settles the last.
abstract.cn: 想象一排立着的多米诺，近得第一张就能决定最后一张。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase with no missing step and no extra one.
abstract.cn: 想象一段楼梯，既没有缺一阶，也没有多一阶。

abstract.en: Picture two maps of the same city that agree on every street.
abstract.cn: 想象同一座城市的两张地图，每条街都对得上。

examples.en: The logical conclusion of the policy is higher taxes.
examples.cn: 这项政策合乎逻辑的结论是更高的税。

examples.en: Her explanation was logical, but it began from a wrong assumption.
examples.cn: 她的解释合乎逻辑，但出发点是错的假设。

examples.en: Put the chapters in a logical order before you submit.
examples.cn: 交稿前把各章按逻辑顺序排好。

dict_mnemonic.text: log（言辞、理性）+ ical（属于……的）＝ 属于理性规则的 → 合乎逻辑的、合理的。

root: 希腊 logikos「擅长言辞或推理的」，来自 logos「词、言语、说明、理性」，其背后的动词 legein 意为「说、挑出、收集」；更深来源不确定。经拉丁与古法语进入英语。同族有 logic、logician、dialogue、analogy。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one chain of steps. It can be a formal derivation, a sensible choice, a branch of study, a self-consistent whole, the step that seems forced, the mind that keeps order, a machine's operation on true and false, or simply an arrangement with a place for everything.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条步骤链展开。它可以是形式推导、明智的选择、一门学科、自洽的整体、显得非如此不可的一步、保持次序的心智、机器对真假的运算，或仅仅是各得其所的排列。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain in which every link is fastened to the one before.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条每一环都扣在前一环上的链。

branches.en: RULE AND DISCIPLINE: the valid step, then the subject that studies such steps.
branches.cn: 规则与学科：有效的一步，以及研究这类步骤的科目。

branches.en: OUTSIDE THE PROOF: the same approval given to ordinary good judgment.
branches.cn: 走出证明之外：同样的认可被给了日常的明智判断。

branches.en: COHERENCE AND LAYOUT: parts that do not cancel each other, shown as a visible order.
branches.cn: 自洽与排布：彼此不取消的部分，显现为可见的次序。

branches.en: THE LAST LINK: the step that looks forced rather than chosen.
branches.cn: 最后一环：看起来不是被选择、而是被逼出的那一步。

branches.en: KEEPER AND MACHINE: the person whose thinking keeps order, and the circuit that runs on the same rules.
branches.cn: 守序者与机器：思维保持次序的人，以及运行在同样规则上的电路。

intro.en: Logical is a Greek-derived adjective carrying a Latin adjective ending, and the root behind it builds a large family in English.
intro.cn: logical 是一个源自希腊语的形容词，带着拉丁形容词词尾，它背后的词根在英语中构成一大批词。

latinIntro.en: Greek supplied the noun for word and reason; Latin and French supplied the endings that turned it into the English adjective and its relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语提供了指「言辞与理性」的名词；拉丁语与法语提供了把它变成英语形容词及其亲属的词尾。

items.example: One noun covers a sentence and the order of the world.
items.exampleCN: 一个名词同时涵盖一句话与世界的秩序。

items.structure: legein (Greek verb, 'to say, gather, pick out')
items.example: Speaking is pictured as picking words out.
items.exampleCN: 说话被描绘为把词挑出来。

items.example: The ending makes an adjective of skill.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾造出表示「擅长」的形容词。

items.example: Logic supplies the rules that reasoning follows.
items.exampleCN: 逻辑提供推理所遵循的规则。

items.example: The argument was logical at every step.
items.exampleCN: 这个论证每一步都合乎逻辑。

items.example: The two claims cannot both be true logically.
items.exampleCN: 这两个主张在逻辑上不可能同时为真。

items.example: A logician tests the form, not the content.
items.exampleCN: 逻辑学家检验形式，而非内容。

items.example: The prefix means 'across', so speech passes between two.
items.exampleCN: 前缀意为「穿过」，言语在两人之间往返。

items.example: The prefix means 'according to', giving a matching of ratios.
items.exampleCN: 前缀意为「按照」，给出比值的对应。

items.example: The ending names disciplines built on ordered speech.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾命名建立在有序言说之上的学科。

derivatives.zh: 逻辑；逻辑学（希腊词根「言辞、理性」，由「说话」转为「推理规则」）
逻辑上；必然地（形容词加副词后缀）
逻辑学家（名词词干加表从业者的后缀）
合乎逻辑的性质（形容词加名词后缀）

definition_zh: 孤独的；寂寞的；偏僻的；荒凉的；孤零零的
definition_en: unhappy because one lacks company; (of a place) far from others and rarely visited; standing apart with nothing similar nearby
core_image: 深夜的公交站牌下，只有一个人影和一条长长的影子
scene: 雪停了，屋檐下的灯还亮着，屋里只有一个人。She felt lonely in the new flat, even though the street outside was full of noise.
sceneCN: 这里是「因缺少陪伴而难受」（第 1 个义项：独自一人时感到寂寞）；句意为虽然外面的街道很吵，她在新公寓里仍然觉得寂寞。

pos.zh: 孤独的；寂寞的；偏僻的；荒凉的

derivatives.zh: lonely 去 y 加 -ness 构成，义为「孤独；寂寞」
由词干 lone 加 -er 构成，义为「独来独往的人」
lonely 的词干，由 alone 截短而来，义为「单独的；无伴的」
由 alone 加 -ness 构成，义为「独自一人的状态」

senses.title: Sad because one has no company
senses.definition: unhappy because one lacks company or close contact with other people
senses.definitionCN: 因为缺少陪伴或与他人的亲近接触而难受
senses.example: He grew lonely after his closest friends moved away.
senses.exampleCN: 最亲近的朋友搬走以后，他变得孤独起来。
senses.why: Lone means being just one, and -ly turns that state into a feeling; the pain comes from having nobody to answer you.
senses.whyCN: lone 意为「只有一个人」，-ly 把这种状态变成一种感受；难受的根源是身边没有人回应自己。

senses.title: Remote and rarely visited
senses.definition: of a place: far from other places, with few people passing through
senses.definitionCN: 指地方远离别处，很少有人经过
senses.example: The farm stood on a lonely stretch of the coast road.
senses.exampleCN: 那座农场孤零零地立在海岸公路的一段上。
senses.why: A place that is one by itself, far from any neighbour, borrows the human word for isolation and turns it into a description of distance.
senses.whyCN: 一个地方独自存在、离任何邻里都远，于是借用了写人的「孤立」一词，把它变成对距离的描述。

senses.title: Standing apart with nothing similar nearby
senses.titleCN: 孤零零的；旁边没有同样的东西
senses.definition: of a thing: standing alone, separated from others of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 指物体单独立着，和同类分开
senses.example: A lonely tree stood at the top of the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 山顶上立着一棵孤零零的树。
senses.why: From people to places and then to objects, the same shape repeats: one thing, no companion, a visible gap around it.
senses.whyCN: 从人扩展到地方，再扩展到物体，重复的是同一个形状：只有一样东西，没有同伴，四周留着一圈看得见的空。

intro.en: Lonely is built from lone, a shortened form of alone, which began as the Old English phrase for all one; the word for one lies underneath all of it.
intro.cn: lonely 由 lone 加后缀构成，而 lone 是 alone 的截短形式；alone 最初是古英语中「全部为一」的说法，底下站着的是表示「一」的词。

items.en: The English word one and Latin unus both descend from a shared Indo-European form for a single unit.
items.cn: 英语的 one 与拉丁语 unus 都来自印欧语系中表示「一个单位」的同一个形式。

items.en: An meant one, and al, meaning all, was joined to it, so al an said all one, that is, entirely by oneself.
items.cn: ān 意为「一」，表示「全部」的 al 加在前面，al an 就是「全部为一」，也就是完完全全只有自己。

items.en: The phrase was written as one word, alone, and speakers later clipped off the first syllable to make lone.
items.cn: 这个短语后来写成一个词 alone，再往后说话的人省掉了开头音节，得到了 lone。

items.en: Adding -ly to lone made lonely, which describes not the fact of being alone but the state of feeling it.
items.cn: 在 lone 后加 -ly 得到 lonely，它描述的不是独处的事实，而是独处带来的状态。

items.en: Modern English uses lonely for people, for remote places and for single objects standing apart from their kind.
items.cn: 现代英语用 lonely 写人、写偏僻的地方，也写单独立着、和同类分开的物体。

note.en: The look-alike group traces the family back to the word for one; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of isolation and emptiness.
note.cn: 形近组沿着「一」这个词把整族词串起来；近义组收表示孤立与空寂的形容词。

entries.definition: Single or without company, used mainly before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 单独的、无伴的，多用在名词前。

entries.definition: By oneself, with nobody else present.
entries.definitionCN: 独自一人，没有其他人在场。

entries.definition: The state or feeling of being lonely.
entries.definitionCN: 孤独的状态或感受。

entries.definition: A person who chooses to spend time alone.
entries.definitionCN: 喜欢独自待着的人。

entries.definition: A chiefly American word close in meaning to lonely.
entries.definitionCN: 主要用于美国英语，意思接近 lonely。

entries.definition: Done alone, or living alone by choice.
entries.definitionCN: 独自做的，或自愿独居的。

entries.definition: Cut off from other people or places.
entries.definitionCN: 与其他人或地方隔绝的。

entries.definition: Empty because everyone has left.
entries.definitionCN: 因为人都离开而空荡的。

entries.definition: Far away from towns and other people.
entries.definitionCN: 远离城镇和人群的。

normalIntro.en: Lonely rests on the old phrase for all one, so the word measures how far a person is from any other voice.
normalIntro.cn: lonely 立在古英语「全部为一」这个说法上，所以这个词量的是一个人离另一个声音有多远。

normal.en: Lonely comes from lone, and lone is alone with its first syllable clipped; alone literally said all one.
normal.cn: lonely 来自 lone，而 lone 是去掉开头音节的 alone；alone 字面就是「全部为一」。

normal.en: Alone states a fact and lonely states a feeling, which is why a person can be alone for a week without feeling lonely.
normal.cn: alone 说的是事实，lonely 说的是感受，所以一个人可以独处一周却不觉得寂寞。

normal.en: Add -ly to lone and you get lonely, the same suffix that builds friendly and lovely from nouns.
normal.cn: 在 lone 后加 -ly 就是 lonely，friendly 和 lovely 也是用同一个后缀从名词变来的。

normal.en: Loneliness adds -ness to lonely, turning a passing mood into a lasting condition.
normal.cn: loneliness 在 lonely 后加 -ness，把一时的情绪变成一种持续的状态。

normal.en: Lonesome is the American cousin; -some carries the sense of full of, so it is full of being alone.
normal.cn: lonesome 是美式英语的近亲；-some 带有「充满」的意味，所以它指「满是独处的感觉」。

abstract.en: All one is a picture before it is a phrase: a person pulling the whole world in until only himself is left.
abstract.cn: 「全部为一」先是一个画面，然后才是一个说法：一个人把整个世界收拢，直到只剩下自己。

abstract.en: A road and a tree can be lonely too, which shows English is willing to lend a human situation to the landscape.
abstract.cn: 一条路、一棵树也能用 lonely，说明英语愿意把人的处境借给风景。

abstract.en: When the lights, the heating and the street noise are all present and the person is still lonely, the word is counting echoes rather than neighbours.
abstract.cn: 灯、暖气和街上的喧闹都在，人却仍然 lonely，说明这个词数的是回应，而不是身边的人。

examples.en: She felt lonely on her first night in the city.
examples.cn: 她在这个城市的第一夜感到孤独。

examples.en: They walked along a lonely road for hours.
examples.cn: 他们在一条荒凉的路上走了几个小时。

examples.en: A lonely tree stood in the middle of the field.
examples.cn: 田野中央立着一棵孤零零的树。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「冷离」——冷冷地离开人群，身边空了，心里也就 lonely。

root: lone 是 alone 的截短形式；alone 由古英语 ān（一）加上 al-（全）构成，字面是「全部为一」，再加 -ly 便成 lonely。词根 ān 与拉丁语 ūnus（一）同出印欧语系。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the state of being only one; it spreads from a person's sadness, to a place with no visitors, to an object with no neighbour.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「只剩一个」的状态；它从人的难受，扩到无人经过的地方，再扩到旁边没有同类的物体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one figure under a street lamp, with a long shadow and no second pair of footsteps.
core.cn: 核心意象：路灯下只有一个人影，影子拉得很长，没有第二串脚步声。

branches.en: a lit window with only one chair at the table

definition_zh: 看；瞧；看起来；显得；目光；一瞥；外观；样子；朝向
definition_en: to direct your eyes towards something; to seem or appear in a certain way; an act of looking, or the appearance of someone or something
core_image: 玻璃柜前，一双眼睛把画上的每一笔都慢慢扫过
scene: 展厅里人不多，一个女孩在画前站了很久。She looked at the painting for a long time before she spoke.
sceneCN: 这里是「把视线投向某物」（第 1 个义项：用眼睛去看）；句意为她在画前看了很久才开口。

pos.zh: 看；瞧；看起来；显得；朝向
看；一瞥；外观；样子

senses.title: To direct the eyes at something
senses.definition: to turn your eyes towards something in order to see it
senses.definitionCN: 把眼睛转向某物，以便看见它
senses.example: Look at the map before you choose a route.
senses.exampleCN: 选路线之前先看看地图。
senses.why: Old English locian named the act of using the eyes, so the physical movement of attention is the base from which the other senses grow.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 lōcian 指的就是用眼睛去看，所以这个把注意力送出去的动作，是其余义项生长的根。

senses.title: To seem or appear a certain way
senses.definition: to seem or appear, judged from what the eye can see
senses.definitionCN: 根据眼睛能看到的情况作出判断；显得
senses.example: The soup looks hot enough to burn your tongue.
senses.exampleCN: 这汤看上去烫得能烫到舌头。
senses.why: What a thing looks like is the evidence the eye gathers, and English lets that evidence become a judgement, so a visible clue turns into a claim about the thing.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西看起来如何，是眼睛收集到的证据；英语让这份证据直接变成判断，于是看得见的线索变成了对事物的说法。

senses.title: The appearance of someone or something
senses.definition: the appearance of a person or thing, especially the impression it makes
senses.definitionCN: 人或物呈现出来的样子，尤指它给人的印象
senses.example: She gave the old bike a new look with a coat of paint.
senses.exampleCN: 她刷了一层漆，让那辆旧自行车有了新样子。
senses.why: The noun takes the verb's picture and fixes it: a look is what a thing presents to anyone who glances at it.
senses.whyCN: 名词把动词的画面固定下来：一个 look 就是一样东西呈现在任何瞥见它的人眼里的样子。

senses.title: A single act of looking
senses.definition: one short act of directing the eyes at something
senses.definitionCN: 把目光投向某物的一次短暂动作
senses.example: A quick look at the clock told him he was late.
senses.exampleCN: 他瞟了一眼钟，就知道自己迟到了。
senses.why: Counting the action gives a small unit, one turn of the eyes, which is why a look can be quick, long or stolen.
senses.whyCN: 把动作数出来就得到一个小单位，也就是眼睛转动的一回，所以 a look 可以是快的、久的，也可以是偷偷投过去的。

senses.title: To face a particular direction
senses.definition: of a building or room: to have its front or opening towards a place
senses.definitionCN: 指建筑或房间的正面或开口朝向某个方向
senses.example: The kitchen looks out over the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房的窗子朝向花园。
senses.why: A building has a front, and the front is where it faces; English describes that facing as looking, as if the house had eyes.
senses.whyCN: 建筑有正面，正面就是它朝向的一边；英语把这种朝向说成 looking，仿佛房子也长了眼睛。

intro.en: Look goes back to an Old English verb for using the eyes, and its deeper origin is uncertain; the sense of seeming grew from the visible evidence a thing offers.
intro.cn: look 可以追到古英语中表示「用眼睛看」的动词，更早的来源不确定；「显得」这一义则从事物给出的可见证据上长出来。

items.en: Related forms appear in other West Germanic languages, but no earlier common source is established beyond doubt.
items.cn: 其他西日耳曼语中能看到相关的形式，但更早的共同来源并没有定论。

items.en: Locian meant to see or to look, and it described the act of turning the eyes towards something.
items.cn: lōcian 意为看、望，描述的是把眼睛转向某物的动作。

items.en: The verb survived as loken, and its spelling slowly moved towards the modern form with oo.
items.cn: 这个动词在中古英语中写作 lōken，拼写慢慢向带 oo 的现代形式靠拢。

items.en: Writers began using look with an adjective after it, so that a thing could look tired, fresh or dangerous.
items.cn: 早期现代英语的作者开始让 look 后面接形容词，于是一样东西可以看起来疲惫、新鲜或危险。

items.en: The word now covers seeing, seeming, appearance and direction, and it builds a large family of compounds.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词覆盖看、显得、外观和朝向，并构成一大族复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group is formed with out, on and alike; the near-meaning group gathers the main verbs of seeing and seeming.
note.cn: 形近组由 out、on、alike 等成分与 look 组合而成；近义组收表示看与显得的主要动词。

normalIntro.en: Look is a plain verb of the eyes that grew a second life as a verb of judgement, so seeing and seeming share one form.
normalIntro.cn: look 本是眼睛的动词，后来又长出判断的用法，于是「看见」和「显得」共用同一个形式。

normal.en: Old English locian meant to use the eyes, and the modern verb continues that physical act without interruption.
normal.cn: 古英语 lōcian 意为用眼睛看，现代动词直接继承了这一身体动作。

normal.en: Look after is literally to look behind someone, which is what caring for a person feels like: your eyes keep following them.
normal.cn: look after 字面是「在某人后面看」，照看一个人正是这种感觉：目光一直跟着他。

normal.en: Look forward to points the eyes ahead, so the phrase means waiting for something that has not happened yet.
normal.cn: look forward to 把眼睛朝前放，所以这个短语指等待还没发生的事。

normal.en: A lookout is look plus out: the person or place that watches outward for what is coming.
normal.cn: lookout 是 look 加 out：向外看、留意有什么过来的人或地方。

normal.en: Lookalike joins look and alike, two things that look the same without being the same.
normal.cn: lookalike 把 look 和 alike 拼在一起：看着一样，其实并不是同一个。

abstract.en: Looking is attention sent outward, which is why the verb so often needs at, for or into to say where the eyes land.
abstract.cn: 看是把注意力送出去，所以这个动词常要带 at、for 或 into，说明目光落在哪里。

abstract.en: One word for seeing and for seeming tells us how much English trusts the eye as a judge.
abstract.cn: 「看」和「显得」共用一个词，说明英语很相信眼睛作出的判断。

abstract.en: The look of a thing is the face it turns towards the world, so style, mood and expression can all fit inside the word.
abstract.cn: 一样东西的 look 是它朝向世界的那一面，所以风格、气氛和神情都能装进这个词。

examples.en: Look at the sky before you decide to go.
examples.cn: 出门之前先看看天。

examples.en: The room looks much bigger without the extra chairs.
examples.cn: 少了那几把多余的椅子，房间看起来大得多。

examples.en: He took one look at the letter and left the room.
examples.cn: 他看了一眼那封信，就离开了房间。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the eye turned outward; from that come the judgement of seeming, the noun for appearance, the counted glance, and the facing of a building.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是向外转的眼睛；由此长出「显得」的判断、表示外观的名词、被数出来的一瞥，以及建筑的朝向。

senses.definitionCN: 绳子、金属丝或线条弯回来、彼此交叉或几乎交叉时形成的形状
senses.example: She made a loop with the rope and hung it on the hook.
senses.exampleCN: 她用绳子打了个环，挂在钩子上。
senses.why: A line bent back on itself leaves the eye with a closed figure; the shape, not the material, is what the word first names.
senses.whyCN: 一条线弯回自身，在眼里留下一个闭合的图形；这个词最先命名的不是材料，而是这个形状。

senses.title: A ring used for fastening
senses.definition: a small ring or curved strip fixed to something so that a belt, hook or cord can pass through it
senses.definitionCN: 固定在物体上的小环或弧形条，用来让腰带、钩子或绳索引穿过去
senses.example: The belt goes through a leather loop at the waist.
senses.exampleCN: 腰带从腰间的一个皮环里穿过去。
senses.why: Once a rope's closed curve can hold another thing, the same outline can be sewn or moulded onto an object; the ring stays because it still does the holding.
senses.whyCN: 一根绳子的闭合曲线一旦能套住别的东西，同样的轮廓就可以缝上或铸在物件上；环之所以留下，是因为它仍在承担「套住」这件事。

senses.title: A repeated cycle in a process or program
senses.definition: a set of instructions or events that returns to its starting point and repeats, especially in computing
senses.definitionCN: 一组回到起点并不断重复的指令或事件，尤用于计算机领域
senses.example: The program got stuck in a loop and printed the same line forever.
senses.exampleCN: 程序卡在循环里，一直打印同一行。
senses.why: A closed curve has no exit; when the steps of a process follow one another back to the start, the path of that process looks like the curve, so the repeat borrows the name.
senses.whyCN: 闭合的曲线没有出口；当一个过程的步骤依次回到起点，这个过程走过的路径就像那条曲线，于是重复也借用了这个名字。

senses.title: To form a curve or ring
senses.definition: to make something into a curve that closes on itself, or to be shaped in that way
senses.definitionCN: 把某物弄成闭合的曲线，或本身以那种形状存在
senses.example: Loop the cable twice around the frame before tightening it.
senses.exampleCN: 把缆线在架子上绕两圈再拉紧。
senses.why: The noun names the closed shape; the verb turns that shape into an action and asks what the hands are doing to the material.
senses.whyCN: 名词命名的是闭合的形状；动词把这个形状变成动作，问的是双手正在对材料做什么。

senses.title: To move around something in a curve
senses.definition: to travel in a curve that goes round something and often comes back towards the starting side
senses.definitionCN: 沿着一条绕过某物、常常又回到出发一侧的曲线行进
senses.example: The path loops around the pond and returns to the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 这条小路绕过池塘，又回到门口。
senses.why: A traveller going round a hill traces the same closed line on the ground, so the name of the shape becomes a verb for the route.
senses.whyCN: 绕山而行的人在土地上画出的正是同一条闭合线，于是形状的名字变成了路线上的动词。

intro.en: Loop is first recorded in Middle English for a bend in a rope; where the word came from is still debated, and the modern technical senses grew out of that rope ring.
intro.cn: loop 最早见于中古英语，指绳子上的一处弯折；它的来源至今仍有争论，现代的技术义项都是从那个绳环生长出来的。

items.en: The earliest recorded loop names a bend or fold in a rope or cord, not yet a perfect circle.
items.cn: 最早记录的 loop 指绳子或细索上的一个弯折，还不一定是完整的圆。

items.en: One common suggestion links it to Old Norse hlaup, a leap, through the running knot that a pulled rope forms; another points to Middle Dutch loopen, to run. Neither is certain.
items.cn: 一种常见说法认为它与古诺斯语 hlaup（跳跃）有关，因为拉紧的活结会形成环；另一种说法指向中古荷兰语 loopen（奔跑）。两说都不确定。

items.en: By the sixteenth century loop covered any ring-shaped curve, including loops of ribbon, metal and lace.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，loop 已泛指任何环状曲线，包括丝带、金属和花边形成的圈。

items.en: Railways and telegraphy gave loop a closed route or circuit, as in a loop line that turns back on itself.
items.cn: 铁路与电报事业给 loop 添上「闭合路线、回路」的义项，如折返回原处的环线。

items.en: Computing made the repeated instruction cycle a loop, and sound and video added the sense of playing a passage over and over.
items.cn: 计算机把反复执行的指令周期叫作 loop，声音与影像又添上「反复播放一段内容」的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and compounds built on loop; the near-meaning group gathers words for rings, coils and repeated cycles.
note.cn: 形近组收由 loop 构成的变形与复合词；近义组收表示环、盘绕与循环的词。

entries.definition: Silly or slightly crazy, as if one's thoughts have gone round in circles.
entries.definitionCN: 由 loop 加 -y 构成，义为「古怪的；脑子像绕成圈一样糊涂的」。

entries.definition: The act of forming a loop, or a repeated replay of a passage.
entries.definitionCN: 由 loop 加 -ing 构成，义为「成环；循环播放」。

entries.definition: A small opening in a wall, and later a gap in rules that lets someone avoid them.
entries.definitionCN: 由 loop 与 hole 复合，原指墙上的窄孔，后指规则中的「漏洞」。

entries.definition: A path or signal that returns to its own source.
entries.definitionCN: 由 loop 与 back 复合，义为「回环；环回路径」。

entries.definition: A round shape or circular object, especially one with an open centre.
entries.definitionCN: 环；圆圈；强调圆形本身，不一定有交叉或回环。

entries.definition: A length of wire or rope wound into a series of circles.
entries.definitionCN: 盘绕的一圈；强调材料被螺旋状连续卷起。

entries.definition: A set of events that repeats in the same order.
entries.definitionCN: 循环；周期；强调事件按同样顺序重复，不强调形状。

entries.definition: A closed route that starts and ends at the same place, or a path for electric current.
entries.definitionCN: 闭合路线；电路；强调起点与终点相接的一整圈。

normalIntro.en: The word is anchored in a rope bent back into a ring, and its family keeps returning to circles, repeats and routes that come back.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词锚定在一根弯回成环的绳子上，它的同族词反复回到圆圈、重复以及折返回来的路线。

normal.en: Two o letters in the middle of loop look like two joined rings, which is exactly the shape the word names.
normal.cn: loop 中间的两个字母 o 像两个相连的圆圈，正好是这个单词所指的形状。

normal.en: In the loop means inside a circle of people who know something; out of the loop means left outside that circle.
normal.cn: in the loop 指在知道内情的圈子里；out of the loop 指被留在圈子外面。

normal.en: A computer loop repeats the same instructions until a condition stops it, because a closed path keeps returning to where it began.
normal.cn: 计算机的 loop 会反复执行同样的指令直到条件终止，因为闭合的路径总是回到起点。

normal.en: Loop back is what a road or a signal does when it turns round and comes back towards its source.
normal.cn: loop back 就是道路或信号折返、朝源头回来时所做的动作。

normal.en: Loopy adds -y to loop: thoughts that go round and round without reaching a clear end sound slightly mad.
normal.cn: loopy 在 loop 后加 -y：想法一圈圈绕却到不了清楚的终点，听起来就有点古怪。

abstract.en: A loop has no obvious exit; walking it once only brings you back to the same gate.
abstract.cn: 一个环没有明显的出口；走一圈只会把你带回同一扇门。

abstract.en: A circle of information works the same way: those inside hear everything, those outside hear nothing.
abstract.cn: 信息的圈子也是一样：圈内的人什么都听得到，圈外的人什么都听不到。

abstract.en: Habits are loops too, which is why breaking one means cutting the path rather than walking it faster.
abstract.cn: 习惯也是环，所以改掉一个习惯要切断路径，而不是走得更快。

examples.en: The road loops around the hill before joining the highway.
examples.cn: 这条路绕过山丘之后才接上公路。

examples.en: The program got stuck in a loop and printed the same line forever.
examples.cn: 程序卡在循环里，一直打印同一行。

examples.en: She made a loop with the rope and hung it on the hook.
examples.cn: 她用绳子打了个环，挂在钩子上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卢普」——绳子一绕就圈成个环；loop 就是环、圈，也指循环。

root: 中古英语 loop 最早指绳子上的弯折；词源一般认为与古诺斯语 hlaup（跳跃）或中古荷兰语 loopen（奔跑）有关，但两说都无定论；现代又引申出循环、环线、回路等义。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a line that bends back into a ring; the senses divide into the shape, the fastening ring, the repeated cycle, the act of forming a loop, and the act of travelling round.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一条弯回成环的线；义项由此分出形状本身、起固定作用的环、反复的循环、把东西弄成环的动作，以及绕行一圈的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope bent into a circle, its two ends almost meeting like a knot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段绳子弯成圆圈，两头几乎相接，像一个刚打好的结。

branches.en: a rope curled into a ring on the floor
branches.cn: 地上盘成一圈的一段绳子

branches.en: a leather ring sewn onto a belt
branches.cn: 缝在腰带上的一个皮环

branches.en: a program printing the same line again and again
branches.cn: 程序一遍遍打印同一行

branches.cn: 双手把缆线弯成一个圈

branches.en: a path going round a pond and back to the gate
branches.cn: 小路绕池塘一圈回到门口

intro.en: Loop is a single stem, but its compounds and suffixes show how a rope ring grew into computing and media.
intro.cn: loop 本身是一个不可再拆的词干，但它的复合词与后缀显示了绳环如何长进计算机与影音领域。

latinIntro.en: Loop has no recorded Latin source; its origin is uncertain and is usually discussed through Germanic words, so no Latin family is listed.
latinIntro.cn: loop 没有可靠的拉丁语来源；它的来源不确定，通常放在日耳曼语词里讨论，因此不列拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 松的；不紧的；宽松的；不受约束的；不严谨的；释放
definition_en: not firmly fixed or tied, not fitting closely, free from control or restraint, not strict or precise, or to set something free
core_image: 一根原本绷紧的绳子忽然松下来，绳结松垮地垂在木桩边
scene: 清晨的码头上，一条小船的缆绳在桩上松了半圈，船身轻轻晃动。The rope came loose during the night and the boat drifted a little.
sceneCN: 这里 loose 是「松的、不紧的」（第 1 个义项：没有牢牢固定）；句意为夜里缆绳松了，船稍微漂开。图中可辨识物件：码头、缆绳、木桩、小船。

pos.zh: 松的；不紧的；宽松的；不受约束的；不严谨的
释放；放开；射出

collocations.zh: 未了结的细节；松散的线头

由 loose 加 -en 构成，义为「使变松；松开」

senses.title: Not firmly fixed or tied
senses.definition: not held tightly in place, so that it can move, slip or come off
senses.definitionCN: 没有被牢牢固定在原位，因此会移动、滑动或脱落
senses.example: One of the screws is loose and the shelf wobbles.
senses.exampleCN: 有一颗螺丝松了，架子摇摇晃晃。
senses.why: The core image is tension gone slack: what should grip no longer grips, so the first sense names anything that can move because it is not held fast.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是张力消失、变松：本该咬住的不再咬住，所以第一个义项指任何因为没被牢牢固定而能移动的东西。

senses.title: Not fitting closely
senses.definition: of clothes or coverings, larger than the body so that it does not press against it
senses.definitionCN: 指衣服或覆盖物比身体大，不会紧贴身体
senses.example: He wore a loose shirt to the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 他穿着一件宽松的衬衫去面试。
senses.why: When cloth stops pressing on the body, the same slackness that lets a screw slip lets air move under a garment; the sense moves from fastening to fit.
senses.whyCN: 当布料不再压住身体，让螺丝滑动的那种松弛便让空气能在衣服下面流动；义项从「固定」转到「合身程度」。

senses.title: Free from control or restraint
senses.definition: not kept in a cage, prison or strict system, and able to move or act freely
senses.definitionCN: 没有被关在笼子、监狱或严格体系里，能够自由移动或行动
senses.example: The gate was left open and the dog got loose.
senses.exampleCN: 大门没关，狗跑了出去。
senses.why: A thing not tied down is also not controlled; once the physical rope is gone, the word can describe anyone or anything escaping restraint.
senses.whyCN: 没有被捆住的东西也不受控制；一旦具体的绳子消失，这个词就能形容任何摆脱约束的人或物。

senses.title: Not strict or precise
senses.definition: of language, rules or thinking, not exact and allowing more than one interpretation
senses.definitionCN: 指语言、规则或思考不精确，允许不止一种解释
senses.example: The article gives only a loose definition of the term.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章只给这个术语下了一个宽泛的定义。
senses.why: A tight knot leaves no room to move; a statement that leaves room to move is felt to be tied just as loosely, so precision becomes the thing that is not fastened down.
senses.whyCN: 系紧的结不留活动的余地；一句留有余地的话也被觉得系得同样松，于是精确性成了那个没被固定住的东西。

senses.title: To set free or let go
senses.definition: to release an animal, a person or a held object, or to fire an arrow or shot
senses.definitionCN: 放开动物、人或握住的物体，也可指射出箭或子弹
senses.example: The keeper loosed the dogs at sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 日落后，看守人把狗放开了。
senses.why: The adjective describes the state of being untied; the verb is the act that produces that state, so the same word becomes the hand opening.
senses.whyCN: 形容词描述的是「已被解开」的状态；动词则是产生这种状态的动作，于是同一个词变成了张开的手。

intro.en: Loose is generally traced to a Germanic adjective for slackness and freedom; English later built loosely, loosen and looseness on it.
intro.cn: loose 一般认为源自一个表示松弛与自由的日耳曼语形容词；英语后来在它之上构成了 loosely、loosen 与 looseness。

items.en: The adjective is generally traced to Old Norse lauss, meaning loose, free or dissolute, which entered English during the Norse settlements.
items.cn: 这个形容词一般认为源自古诺斯语 lauss，意为松的、自由的、放纵的，在诺斯人定居时期进入英语。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form means loose or free; German los and Dutch los are close relatives, and the English suffix -less grows from the same family.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形式意为松的、自由的；德语 los 与荷兰语 los 是近亲，英语后缀 -less 也出自同一词族。

items.en: Middle English loose appears as an adjective for what is not bound, and a verb meaning to set free grows beside it.
items.cn: 中古英语的 loose 已是形容词，指没有被捆住的东西；旁边又长出表示「释放」的动词。

items.en: The word spreads from ropes and cages to clothes, morals and language, giving phrases such as loose woman and loose translation.
items.cn: 这个词从绳索与笼子扩展到衣服、品行与语言，产生 loose woman 与 loose translation 之类的说法。

items.en: Modern English keeps the physical and abstract senses side by side and builds the family loosely, loosen and looseness; it is a different word from lose, which means to misplace or be deprived of.
items.cn: 现代英语让具体的与抽象的义项并排存在，并构成 loosely、loosen、looseness 等同族词；它与表示「丢失、失去」的 lose 是不同的词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers family forms and the easily confused lose; the near-meaning group gathers words for slackness, loose fit and freedom.
note.cn: 形近组收同族形式以及容易混淆的 lose；近义组收表示松弛、宽松与自由的词。

entries.definition: In a slack, relaxed or inexact way.
entries.definitionCN: 由 loose 加 -ly 构成，义为「松散地；不严格地」。

entries.definition: To make or become less tight.
entries.definitionCN: 由 loose 加 -en 构成，义为「使变松；松开」。

entries.definition: The quality or state of being loose.
entries.definitionCN: 由 loose 加 -ness 构成，义为「松弛；松散」。

entries.definition: To no longer have something, or to fail to keep it.
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写和读音相近，词源不同；义为「丢失；失去」。

entries.definition: Not tight, and lacking the usual tension.
entries.definitionCN: 松弛的；强调绳索或肌肉缺少张力，与 loose 近义。

entries.definition: Of clothes, very wide and hanging loosely.
entries.definitionCN: 衣服宽大下垂的；多指版型，不指固定是否牢固。

entries.definition: Not controlled or limited by another person or system.
entries.definitionCN: 自由的；强调不受人或制度限制，不指物理松紧。

entries.definition: Not strict enough in enforcing rules.
entries.definitionCN: 松懈的；多指规则执行不严，源自不同词根。

normalIntro.en: The word is anchored in a Germanic adjective for slackness and freedom, and its family keeps returning to things that are not held tight.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词锚定在一个表示松弛与自由的日耳曼语形容词上，同族词反复回到没有被紧紧固定住的东西。

normal.en: Loose starts in Old Norse lauss, a word for free as well as slack; the physical and the social senses were there from the beginning.
normal.cn: loose 源自古诺斯语 lauss，这个词既指松弛也指自由；具体的与社会的义项从一开始就都在。

normal.en: The suffix -less comes from the same Germanic family, which is why less and loose both carry the idea of being without.
normal.cn: -less 这个后缀出自同一日耳曼词族，所以 less 与 loose 都带着「没有、缺少」的意思。

normal.en: Loosen adds -en to loose and means to make less tight; loosely adds -ly and describes the manner.
normal.cn: loosen 在 loose 后加 -en，表示「使变松」；loosely 加 -ly，描述做事的方式。

normal.en: Loose change is coins carried loose in a pocket, not fastened into a wallet or roll.
normal.cn: loose change 是散放在口袋里、没有捆进钱包或纸卷的零钱。

normal.en: Do not confuse loose with lose: loose is slack, lose is to no longer have something.
normal.cn: 不要把 loose 与 lose 弄混：loose 是松，lose 是失去某物。

abstract.en: A knot that has gone slack can still look tied, which is why loose rules and loose talk are hard to notice at first.
abstract.cn: 松掉的结看上去仍像系着，所以宽松的规则与随意的言辞起初不容易被察觉。

abstract.en: Freedom and slackness share one word because both mean that nothing is holding you in place.
abstract.cn: 自由与松弛共用一个词，因为两者都意味着没有东西把你固定住。

abstract.en: A loose end is not a failure; it is simply a thread the story has not tied yet.
abstract.cn: 松着的线头不是失败，它只是故事还没系上的一根线。

examples.en: One of the screws is loose and the shelf wobbles.
examples.cn: 有一颗螺丝松了，架子摇摇晃晃。

examples.en: He wore a loose shirt to the interview.
examples.cn: 他穿着一件宽松的衬衫去面试。

examples.en: The gate was left open and the dog got loose.
examples.cn: 大门没关，狗跑了出去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「露丝」——衣服露在外头，松松垮垮；loose 就是松的、宽松的。

root: 一般认为源自古诺斯语 lauss（松的、自由的），与古英语 leas（缺少、虚假）同属一个日耳曼词族，并衍生出 -less；没有可靠的拉丁同族词。注意与 lose（丢失）区分。

sensesIntro.en: The core is tension released; the senses divide into physical slackness, loose fit, freedom from control, imprecise wording, and the act of setting something free.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是张力被放开；义项由此分出物理上的松弛、衣服的宽松、不受控制、措辞不精确，以及把某物放开的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope that was taut going slack, its knot drooping beside the post.

definition_zh: 松散地；不紧地；宽大地；不严格地；大致地
definition_en: in a way that is not tight or close, not fitting closely, or not strictly and precisely
core_image: 一件宽大的外套松松地搭在椅背上，两只袖子垂下来
scene: 排练室里，几个人站得很开，动作只是大致跟着节拍。The dancers moved loosely, as if the music were only a suggestion.
sceneCN: 这里 loosely 是「松散地、不严格地」（第 3 个义项：不严格、大致地）；句意为舞者动作松散，好像音乐只是建议。图中可辨识物件：排练室、舞者、节拍。

senses.title: In a way that is not tight
senses.definition: with little tension, so that something can move or slip
senses.definitionCN: 张力很小，因此某物可以移动或滑动
senses.example: She tied the rope loosely around the post.
senses.exampleCN: 她把绳子松松地系在柱子上。
senses.why: The adverb takes the adjective's physical slackness and turns it into the manner of an action: the hand does not pull hard.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把形容词的物理松弛转成动作的方式：手没有用力去拉。

senses.title: In a way that does not fit closely
senses.definition: of clothing, worn so that it hangs away from the body
senses.definitionCN: 指衣服穿着时离开身体、垂下来
senses.example: He wore his coat loosely over his shoulders.
senses.exampleCN: 他把外套松松地披在肩上。
senses.why: Loose cloth hangs; the adverb describes how the garment sits, so fit becomes the second branch.
senses.whyCN: 宽松的布料会垂下来；副词描述衣服如何罩在身上，于是「合身程度」成为第二条分支。

senses.title: Not strictly or precisely
senses.definition: without exact limits, so that the meaning is approximate rather than exact
senses.definitionCN: 没有精确的界限，因此含义是大致的，而非准确的
senses.example: The film is loosely based on a true story.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影大致根据一个真实故事改编。
senses.why: When rules or facts are not pinned down, the manner of holding them is the same as holding a rope without pulling it tight.
senses.whyCN: 当规则或事实没有被钉死，握住它们的方式就像握着一根没有拉紧的绳子。

senses.title: In a loose or unconnected structure
senses.definition: of a group, text or arrangement, with parts not closely joined or ordered
senses.definitionCN: 指群体、文本或安排中的各部分没有紧密连接或排列
senses.example: The chapters are loosely connected by a single theme.
senses.exampleCN: 各章只由一条单一的主题松散地串起来。
senses.why: Parts that are not bound together stay separate; the adverb describes the gaps between them rather than the tightness of any one part.
senses.whyCN: 没有被捆在一起的部分保持分离；副词描述的是它们之间的空隙，而不是某一部分本身有多紧。

intro.en: Loosely is an English adverb made from loose plus -ly; the base word is Germanic, and its senses move from slack rope to inexact description.
intro.cn: loosely 是由 loose 加 -ly 构成的英语副词；词基属于日耳曼语族，义项从松弛的绳子走向不精确的描述。

items.en: The base adjective is generally traced to Old Norse lauss, meaning slack or free.
items.cn: 词基形容词一般认为源自古诺斯语 lauss，意为松的、自由的。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic source also gives German los and the English suffix -less.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语来源也给出德语 los 与英语后缀 -less。

items.en: Middle English used loos or loose as an adjective before the adverb was formed.
items.cn: 在副词形成之前，中古英语已用 loos 或 loose 作形容词。

items.en: The adverb suffix -ly descends from Old English -lice, and loosely appears as loose plus that suffix.
items.cn: 副词后缀 -ly 源自古英语 -lice，loosely 就是 loose 加上这个后缀。

items.en: Modern English extends the adverb from the manner of tying to the accuracy of a claim, so loosely based on becomes a common phrase.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个副词从系绳的方式扩展到陈述的准确程度，于是 loosely based on 成为常见说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adjective, verb and noun of the same family plus the confusing lose; the near-meaning group gathers words for approximation and slackness.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词族的形容词、动词与名词，外加容易混淆的 lose；近义组收表示近似与松弛的词。

abstract.en: A loosely worded promise leaves room for escape, and room for escape is exactly what the word describes.

abstract.en: Loosely does not mean carelessly; it means the grip is light enough to let the thing breathe.

definition_zh: 松开；使变松；放松；放宽；变松
definition_en: to make something less tight, to relax a part of the body, to make rules or controls less strict, to weaken a connection, or to become less tight
core_image: 一只手捏住拧得太紧的瓶盖，慢慢往回拧，指节不再发白
scene: 厨房里，一只拧得太紧的瓶盖卡住了，他换了个手势慢慢往回拧。He loosened the cap after a few turns and the jar opened easily.
sceneCN: 这里 loosen 是「松开、使变松」（第 1 个义项：让某物不再紧）；句意为拧了几圈后他把瓶盖拧松，罐子很容易打开。图中可辨识物件：厨房、瓶盖、罐子。

pos.zh: 松开；使变松；放松；放宽；变松

senses.title: To make something less tight
senses.definition: to reduce the tension on a fastening, a screw, a knot or a grip so that it can move or be removed
senses.definitionCN: 减小扣件、螺丝、绳结或握持上的张力，使它能够移动或被取下
senses.example: He loosened the lid with the help of a cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 他借一块布把盖子拧松了。
senses.why: The verb takes the adjective loose and adds the suffix -en, which means to make; the first sense is simply to put an object into that slack state.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词由形容词 loose 加后缀 -en 构成，而 -en 意为「使……」；第一个义项就是把某物放进那种松弛状态。

senses.title: To relax a part of the body
senses.definition: to make a muscle, joint or posture less tense
senses.definitionCN: 让肌肉、关节或姿势不再那么紧张
senses.example: Roll your shoulders and loosen your neck.
senses.exampleCN: 转一转肩膀，放松脖子。
senses.why: Muscles held too long become tight like a clamped fastening; relaxing them is the same reduction of tension applied to the body.
senses.whyCN: 肌肉保持太久会像卡紧的扣件一样发僵；放松它们，就是把同样的「减小张力」用在身体上。

senses.title: To make rules or controls less strict
senses.definition: to reduce the force of a rule, a limit or a form of control
senses.definitionCN: 减弱规则、限制或某种控制的力度
senses.example: The school loosened its dress code last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校去年放宽了着装规定。
senses.why: A rule works like a band holding behaviour in place; making it less strict is pictured as letting that band go slack.
senses.whyCN: 规则就像一条把行为固定住的带子；让规则不那么严，就被想成把这条带子放松。

senses.title: To weaken a connection or bond
senses.definition: to make a relationship, alliance or link less firm
senses.definitionCN: 使关系、联盟或联系变得不那么牢固
senses.example: Time and distance had loosened the bond between the old friends.
senses.exampleCN: 时间与距离让两位老朋友之间的情谊松动了。
senses.why: A bond is imagined as something tied; when it stops being tight, the people or groups it joined can move apart.
senses.whyCN: 情谊被想象成系在一起的东西；当它不再紧，被它连起来的人或群体就能彼此走开。

senses.title: To become less tight
senses.definition: of a fastening, grip or hold, to become less tight without an outside agent
senses.definitionCN: 指扣件、握持或抓握在没有外力的情况下自己变得不那么紧
senses.example: The rope loosened as the rain soaked through it.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水浸透之后，绳子自己松开了。
senses.why: The same verb covers both sides of the change: a hand can loosen a knot, and a wet knot can loosen on its own, because English does not mark who causes the slackening.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词覆盖变化的两端：手可以松开一个结，湿透的结也能自己变松，因为英语并不标明是谁造成了这种松弛。

intro.en: Loosen is an English verb built on the Germanic adjective loose plus a suffix meaning to make; it describes reduced tightness rather than complete freedom.
intro.cn: loosen 是由日耳曼语形容词 loose 加上表示「使……」的后缀构成的英语动词；它描述的是紧度减小，而不是彻底获得自由。

items.en: The family begins with the Germanic adjective for loose, generally traced to Old Norse lauss.
items.cn: 这个词族始于表示「松的」的日耳曼语形容词，一般认为可上溯到古诺斯语 lauss。

items.en: The reconstructed source also underlies German los and the English suffix -less.
items.cn: 重构的来源也支撑着德语 los 与英语后缀 -less。

items.en: Middle English had the adjective and a verb loose meaning to set free.
items.cn: 中古英语已有这个形容词，也有表示「释放」的动词 loose。

items.en: The verb suffix -en descends from Old English -nian and forms verbs such as strengthen, widen and loosen, meaning to make or become.
items.cn: 动词后缀 -en 源自古英语 -nian，构成 strengthen、widen、loosen 这类表示「使……、变得……」的动词。

items.en: Modern English keeps loosen for reducing tightness and loose for setting free, a division that the two words now share.
items.cn: 现代英语让 loosen 表示「减小紧度」，让 loose 表示「释放」，两个词如今分担了这一分工。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adjective, adverb and noun of the same family plus the confusing lose; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for reducing tension and strictness.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词族的形容词、副词与名词，外加容易混淆的 lose；近义组收表示减小张力与严格程度的动词。

normal.en: Loosen is loose plus -en, the suffix that means to make, so the verb means to make something loose.
normal.cn: loosen 是 loose 加 -en，这个后缀表示「使……」；所以动词的意思就是「使某物变松」。

normal.en: The -en suffix also builds strengthen and widen, which is why loosen belongs with verbs of change.
normal.cn: -en 后缀也构成 strengthen 与 widen，所以 loosen 属于表示变化的动词一类。

normal.en: Loosen a screw, loosen a knot, loosen a grip: each action reduces tension without removing the thing.
normal.cn: 拧松螺丝、松开绳结、放松握持：每个动作都减小张力，却没有把东西拿掉。

normal.en: Loosen up is what people do before exercise, letting tight muscles go slack.
normal.cn: loosen up 就是人们运动前做的事，让紧绷的肌肉松下来。

normal.en: Loose can also be a verb meaning to set free, but loosen is the everyday verb for making less tight.
normal.cn: loose 也能作动词表示「释放」，但 loosen 是日常用来表示「使变松」的动词。

abstract.en: A tight grip protects and controls, but it also tires the hand; loosening is how control makes room for rest.
abstract.cn: 紧握能保护与控制，但也会让手疲劳；松开就是控制为休息让出空间的方式。

abstract.en: Rules can be loosened without being removed, which is why the word describes pressure rather than absence.
abstract.cn: 规则可以被放宽而不必取消，所以这个词描述的是压力，而不是「没有规则」。

abstract.en: To loosen a knot is not to cut it; the rope remains, only the strain is gone.
abstract.cn: 松开一个结并不等于剪断它；绳子还在，只是张力没有了。

examples.en: The cap loosened after a few turns and the jar opened easily.
examples.cn: 拧了几圈后瓶盖松了，罐子很容易打开。

examples.en: He loosened the lid with the help of a cloth.
examples.cn: 他借一块布把盖子拧松了。

examples.en: Roll your shoulders and loosen your neck.
examples.cn: 转一转肩膀，放松脖子。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是张力减小；义项由此分出把物件弄松、放松身体、放宽规则、削弱联系，以及自己变松。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand slowly turning back a tight cap until the knuckles stop whitening.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把拧得太紧的瓶盖慢慢往回拧，直到指节不再发白。

branches.en: a cap turning back under a hand
branches.cn: 一只手把瓶盖往回拧

branches.en: shoulders dropping after a long day
branches.cn: 忙了一天后肩膀垂下来

branches.en: a rule book left open to a softer line
branches.cn: 规则手册翻到较宽松的一页

branches.en: two friends drifting apart without a quarrel
branches.cn: 两位朋友没有争吵却渐渐疏远

branches.en: a wet knot slipping on its own
branches.cn: 湿透的绳结自己滑开

intro.en: The verb is the adjective loose plus the old suffix -en, and the family shares that base with loosely and looseness.
intro.cn: 这个动词是形容词 loose 加上古老的 -en 后缀，同族的 loosely 与 looseness 也共享这个词基。

latinIntro.en: Loosen is an English verb built on loose; the base belongs to Germanic stock, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded.
latinIntro.cn: loosen 是建立在 loose 之上的英语动词；词基属于日耳曼语族，没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。
