definition_zh: 领主；勋爵；贵族；上帝；巨头
definition_en: a man of noble rank or high office; also a title for God and for a dominant figure
core_image: 一名男子站在长桌尽头，把一条条面包分给排队的家人
scene: 中世纪的庄园里，天还没亮，管家已经把当天要分的面包摆上长桌。The lord of the manor watched as each family received its share of bread.
sceneCN: 这里 lord 是「领主、庄园主」（第 2 个义项：封建领主）；句意为庄园领主看着每户人家领到属于自己的那份面包。画面里可认出长桌、面包和排队的人。

pos.zh: 领主；勋爵；贵族；上帝；巨头

derivatives.zh: 由 lord 加形容词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「贵族般的；高傲的」
由 lord 加抽象名词后缀 -ship 构成，义为「领主身份；统治权」
由 land 与 lord 复合而成，义为「地主；房东」
由 over 与 lord 复合而成，义为「最高领主；霸主」

senses.title: A nobleman or a title of rank
senses.definition: a man who holds a noble title, or the title used before his name
senses.definitionCN: 拥有贵族头衔的男子，或用于其名字前的尊称
senses.example: The king granted the title of lord to his most loyal soldier.
senses.exampleCN: 国王把勋爵头衔授予他最忠诚的士兵。
senses.why: In feudal society the word marked a man who held land and rank above ordinary people, so it settled into a formal title.
senses.whyCN: 在封建社会，这个词标记着拥有土地、地位高于平民的男子，于是逐渐固定为一种正式头衔。

senses.title: A feudal master who owns land and controls those who work it
senses.definition: a man who owns land and has power over the people living and working on it
senses.definitionCN: 拥有土地并支配在其上生活、劳作之人的男子
senses.example: The lord of the manor collected rent from every family on his land.
senses.exampleCN: 庄园领主向地上的每一户人家收取地租。
senses.why: The same word for a title also named the practical power behind it: land, rent and the labour of other people.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示头衔的词也指头衔背后的实际权力：土地、地租和别人的劳作。

senses.title: God, or Christ, in religious use
senses.definition: a title used for God or for Christ in Christian speech and prayer
senses.definitionCN: 基督教言语和祈祷中对上帝或基督的称呼
senses.example: They prayed to the Lord for guidance before the journey.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前他们向上帝祈求指引。
senses.why: The Bible was translated into English with this word for a master, so the everyday term for a powerful man was lifted to name the highest power.
senses.whyCN: 《圣经》英译时用这个表示「主人」的词，于是这个日常用来指有权势之人的词被提升去指最高的权能者。

senses.title: A dominant figure in a particular field
senses.definition: a man who is very powerful or influential in a particular activity or industry
senses.definitionCN: 在某一活动或行业中极有权势或影响力的人物
senses.example: He is a lord of the fashion world, with shops in every capital.
senses.exampleCN: 他是时装界的巨头，在每个首都都有店铺。
senses.why: From owning land the word widened to owning influence, so a man who ruled an industry could be called its lord.
senses.whyCN: 从拥有土地扩展到拥有影响力，于是统治一个行业的人也可以被称为该行业的霸主。

intro.en: Lord began as a compound for the keeper of the bread, then grew into a word for masters, nobles and God.
intro.cn: lord 最初是「看管面包的人」的复合词，后来发展为指主人、贵族与上帝。

items.en: The word is first recorded as hlāfweard, a compound of hlāf, bread, and weard, keeper.
items.cn: 这个词最早记作 hlāfweard，由表示面包的 hlāf 与表示看守者的 weard 复合而成。

items.en: Everyday speech shortened hlāfweard to hlāford, and the middle sounds were swallowed.
items.cn: 日常口语把 hlāfweard 缩成 hlāford，中间的音节被吞掉了。

items.en: Middle English lord kept the meaning of a household head and a man of authority.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lord 保留「一家之主」与「有权势的男子」两层意思。

items.en: Under feudalism the word became a title for landowners and nobles, and later for members of the House of Lords.
items.cn: 在封建制度下，这个词成为地主与贵族的头衔，后来又指上议院的成员。

items.en: Modern English uses lord for nobles, for masters, and as a religious title for God.
items.cn: 现代英语用 lord 指贵族、主人，也用作对上帝的宗教称呼。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built from the same bread-and-keeper compound; the near-meaning group gathers words for masters and rulers.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「面包＋看守者」复合词衍生出的词；近义组收表示主人与统治者的词。

entries.definition: The female counterpart of lord, from a compound meaning bread-kneader.
entries.definitionCN: lord 的女性对应词，源自表示「揉面包的人」的复合词。

entries.definition: A shaped mass of baked bread, from the same Old English word for bread.
entries.definitionCN: 一条烤好的面包，来自同一个古英语「面包」词。

entries.definition: Guarding, or a guarded area, from the keeper element in lord.
entries.definitionCN: 守护或受监护的区域，来自 lord 中「看守者」那一部分。

entries.definition: The owner of land or of a rented house.
entries.definitionCN: 地主；房东。

entries.definition: A man who has control over people or a household.
entries.definitionCN: 控制他人或一家之主。

entries.definition: A person who governs a country or a group.
entries.definitionCN: 统治国家或群体的人。

entries.definition: A person of high social rank.
entries.definitionCN: 社会地位高的人。

entries.definition: A king or other supreme ruler.
entries.definitionCN: 国王或其他最高统治者。

normalIntro.en: The word is a compressed compound: bread plus keeper. Its family keeps returning to guarding, owning and ranking above others.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是被压缩的复合词：面包加看守者。它的同族词反复回到看管、拥有与高人一等。

normal.en: Lord began as hlāfweard, the keeper of the bread, so the first lord was simply the one who fed the household.
normal.cn: lord 最初写作 hlāfweard，即看管面包的人，所以最早的领主不过是供养全家的人。

normal.en: The middle of hlāfweard was lost in speech, which is why lord looks nothing like loaf or ward today.
normal.cn: hlāfweard 中间的音在口语里消失了，所以今天的 lord 看起来和 loaf、ward 都不像。

normal.en: Lady is its female counterpart, built from a word for kneading bread, so both titles come from the kitchen.
normal.cn: lady 是它的女性对应词，来自表示揉面包的词，所以两个头衔都出自厨房。

normal.en: Landlord adds land to lord: the man who owns the land and the building on it.
normal.cn: landlord 在 lord 前加 land，指拥有土地及其上房屋的人。

normal.en: Lordship adds -ship: the rank or power that belongs to a lord.
normal.cn: lordship 加后缀 -ship，指属于领主的身份或权力。

abstract.en: A word that once meant the man guarding the bread shows how food was the first form of power.
abstract.cn: 一个曾经指「看管面包的人」的词，说明食物是最初的权力形式。

abstract.en: From feeding a household to ruling a country, the same word simply changed the size of the table.
abstract.cn: 从供养一家人到统治一个国家，同一个词只是换了桌子的尺寸。

abstract.en: Calling God lord keeps the oldest human image of power: someone above who provides and protects.
abstract.cn: 称上帝为 lord，保留了人类最古老的权力形象：在上方供给并保护的人。

examples.en: The lord of the manor watched as each family received its share of bread.
examples.cn: 庄园领主看着每户人家领到属于自己的那份面包。

examples.en: They prayed to the Lord for guidance before the journey.
examples.cn: 出发前他们向上帝祈求指引。

examples.en: The young noble was granted the title of lord after the battle.
examples.cn: 那位年轻贵族战后被授予勋爵头衔。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「老得」——上了年纪、德高望重的老爷，就是 lord。

root: 古英语 hlāfweard（hlāf「面包」+ weard「看守者」）缩合为 hlāford，再演变为 lord；一般认为与「供养、看管家宅」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a man with power over land and people; the senses branch into a noble title, a feudal master, God, and a dominant figure in a field.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是握有土地与人身权力的男子；义项分出贵族头衔、封建领主、上帝，以及某一领域的巨头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a man at the end of a long table, handing out bread to a waiting household.
core.cn: 核心意象：一名男子站在长桌尽头，把面包分给等待的众人。

branches.en: a ceremony where a title is formally granted
branches.cn: 正式授予头衔的仪式

branches.en: a manor where rent is collected from tenants
branches.cn: 向佃户收取地租的庄园

branches.en: hands folded in prayer before a long journey
branches.cn: 长途出发前合拢的祈祷之手

branches.en: a fashion house with shops in every capital
branches.cn: 在每个首都都有店铺的时装帝国

branches.en: the same man holding a title and the land that pays for it
branches.cn: 同一个人既拥有头衔，又拥有供养头衔的土地

intro.en: Lord is a worn-down compound of two Old English nouns, and later English built new words on it with -ly, -ship and further compounding.
intro.cn: lord 是两个古英语名词磨损而成的复合词，后来的英语又用 -ly、-ship 和再次复合造出新词。

latinIntro.en: Lord comes from Germanic bread-and-keeping words, so it has no reliable Latin cognate.
latinIntro.cn: lord 来自日耳曼语表示面包与看守的词，因此没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.example: Old English hlāf survives in the modern word loaf.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 hlāf 保存在现代英语的 loaf 里。

items.example: The weard stood at the door of the hall.
Hlāford named the man who guarded the family's bread.
items.exampleCN: hlāford 指为全家看管面包的人。

items.meaning: a woman of rank or the female head
items.example: The lady of the house greeted the guests.

items.meaningCN: 构成形容词和副词的后缀
items.example: Lordly means noble or proud, built with this suffix.
items.exampleCN: lordly 意为贵族般的或高傲的，由这个后缀构成。

items.example: Lordship means the rank or power of a lord.
items.exampleCN: lordship 指领主的身份或权力。

items.meaning: owner of land or rented property
items.example: The landlord raised the rent last spring.
items.exampleCN: 房东去年春天涨了房租。

items.meaning: the rank, power or territory of a lord
items.example: The lordship passed to his eldest son.
items.exampleCN: 领主之位传给了他的长子。

definition_zh: 卡车；运货汽车；铁路平板车
definition_en: a large road vehicle built for carrying goods; in Britain it is the usual word for a truck
core_image: 一辆方正的运货车停在仓库门口，后厢里堆满纸箱
scene: 清晨的仓库门口，一辆辆运货的重型车排成长队，等着卸下昨夜的货物。A lorry loaded with boxes waited at the gate while the workers checked the list.
sceneCN: 这里 lorry 是「卡车、运货汽车」（第 1 个义项）；句意为一辆装满箱子的卡车停在门口，工人核对清单。画面里可认出仓库门、纸箱和清单。

pos.zh: 卡车；运货汽车；铁路平板车

derivatives.zh: 由 lorry 与 load 复合而成，义为「一卡车的载量」
由 lorry 与 driver 复合而成，义为「卡车司机」

senses.title: A large motor vehicle for carrying goods
senses.definition: a large motor vehicle with an open or enclosed body, built to carry goods on roads
senses.definitionCN: 带有敞篷或封闭车厢、在公路上运送货物的大型机动车辆
senses.example: The lorry carried furniture from the warehouse to the new flat.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆卡车把家具从仓库运到新公寓。
senses.why: When motor vehicles replaced horse carts, the old word for a goods cart was kept for the new machine that did the same job.
senses.whyCN: 当机动车取代马拉车时，原本指运货车的老词被保留下来，用来指干同样工作的新机器。

senses.title: A railway wagon for goods
senses.definition: a flat or open railway wagon used for carrying goods or materials
senses.definitionCN: 用于运送货物或材料的平板或敞篷铁路车皮
senses.example: The coal was loaded onto a lorry waiting on the sidings.
senses.exampleCN: 煤被装上停在侧线的铁路平板车。
senses.why: Before the motor lorry, the same word named the rail wagon that hauled goods inside mines and yards.
senses.whyCN: 在机动车出现之前，同一个词就指矿井和堆场里牵引货物的铁路车皮。

senses.title: A low flat cart, in older British use
senses.definition: a low, flat cart without high sides, used in earlier British English for moving heavy loads
senses.definitionCN: 早期英式英语中指没有高栏、用来搬运重物的低平板车
senses.example: In the old prints, a lorry stands beside the dock with barrels piled on it.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧版画里，一辆低平板车停在码头边，上面堆着木桶。
senses.why: The earliest lorry was simply a low platform on wheels, and that flat shape is where the modern word began.
senses.whyCN: 最早的 lorry 不过是带轮子的低平台，现代这个词正是从那种平板形状开始的。

intro.en: The origin of lorry is uncertain; most accounts trace it to an old British dialect word for dragging or hauling.
intro.cn: lorry 的来源不确定；多数说法把它追溯到古英语方言中表示「拖、拽」的词。

items.en: Lorry first appears in print in the early nineteenth century, naming a low flat cart or wagon.
items.cn: lorry 在十九世纪初首次见于书面记录，指低平板车或货车。

items.en: One common view derives it from dialect lurry, to drag or pull with effort; the source is not certain.
items.cn: 一种常见看法认为它来自方言词 lurry，意为费力地拖拽；但来源并不确定。

items.en: In the railway age lorry named an open goods wagon running on rails.
items.cn: 在铁路时代，lorry 指在轨道上运行的敞篷货车皮。

items.en: When motor vehicles took over, British English moved the word to the road and used it for a motor truck.
items.cn: 当机动车接管运输后，英式英语把这个词移到公路上，用来指机动卡车。

items.en: Today lorry is the everyday British word for a truck, while American English prefers truck.
items.cn: 今天 lorry 是英式英语里指卡车的日常词，而美式英语更常用 truck。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words easily confused with lorry in spelling or sound; the near-meaning group collects other goods vehicles.
note.cn: 形近组收在拼写或读音上容易与 lorry 混淆的词；近义组收其他运货车辆。

entries.definition: A dialect verb meaning to drag or haul; it may lie behind lorry but is a separate form.
entries.definitionCN: 意为拖、拽的方言词；它可能是 lorry 的来源，但本身是另一个词形。

entries.definition: A small wheeled cart or a tram, spelled and sounded somewhat like lorry.
entries.definitionCN: 带轮的小推车或有轨电车，拼写与读音略像 lorry。

entries.definition: As much as a lorry can carry.
entries.definitionCN: 一卡车的载量。

entries.definition: The American word for a large goods vehicle.
entries.definitionCN: 美式英语中大型运货车辆的叫法。

entries.definition: A smaller enclosed vehicle for carrying goods.
entries.definitionCN: 较小的封闭式运货车辆。

entries.definition: A goods vehicle or an open railway truck.
entries.definitionCN: 运货车辆或敞篷铁路货车。

entries.definition: A simple vehicle with wheels, often pulled by an animal.
entries.definitionCN: 有轮子、多用牲畜拉动的简单车辆。

normalIntro.en: The word is short and opaque, so its memory hooks come from its British identity, its railway past and its place among goods vehicles.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词短而难以拆分，所以记忆钩子来自它的英式身份、铁路渊源以及它在运货车辆中的位置。

normal.en: Lorry is the everyday British word for a truck, so remembering the country helps fix the meaning.
normal.cn: lorry 是英式英语里指卡车的日常词，记住它属于英国就能固定词义。

normal.en: Its plural is lorries, because the final y turns to ies after a consonant.
normal.cn: 它的复数是 lorries，因为辅音后的 y 要变成 ies。

normal.en: The word first named a low cart and later a railway wagon, so it moved from rails to roads.
normal.cn: 这个词先指低平板车，后指铁路车皮，因此是从铁轨走向公路。

normal.en: Lorry driver and lorry park are fixed British compounds, which keep the word in daily transport talk.
normal.cn: lorry driver 与 lorry park 是固定的英式复合词，让这个词留在日常运输话题里。

normal.en: A heavy lorry takes a wide lane, which is why the word often appears in road rules.
normal.cn: 重型卡车要占很宽的车道，所以这个词常出现在交通规则里。

abstract.en: A word for a cart on rails becoming the word for a truck shows how transport words follow the machine, not the road.
abstract.cn: 一个指铁轨上货车的词变成指卡车的词，说明交通词汇跟着机器走，而不是跟着路面走。

abstract.en: Lorry and truck name the same thing in two countries, a reminder that synonyms can be national habits.
abstract.cn: lorry 与 truck 在两个国家指同一事物，提醒人近义词也可以是国民习惯。

abstract.en: The flat platform at the start of lorry is still visible in its boxy shape today.
abstract.cn: lorry 起点处的平板形状，今天仍能在它方方正正的车身上看见。

examples.en: The lorry carried furniture from the warehouse to the new flat.
examples.cn: 这辆卡车把家具从仓库运到新公寓。

examples.en: A lorry loaded with boxes waited at the gate.
examples.cn: 一辆装满箱子的卡车等在门口。

examples.en: He drives a heavy lorry across the north of England.
examples.cn: 他驾驶重型卡车穿越英格兰北部。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉里」——一路拉着货物跑的大车，就是 lorry。

root: 来源不确定；一般认为来自英格兰北部方言 lurry（拖、拽），十九世纪初先指低平板车，后指铁路货车与机动卡车；无可靠拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a vehicle built to carry goods; the senses move from a low cart to a railway wagon and then to the motor lorry.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是专门运送货物的车辆；义项从低平板车移到铁路货车，再到机动卡车。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boxy goods vehicle backed up to a warehouse door, its bed full of crates.
core.cn: 核心意象：一辆方正的运货车倒到仓库门口，车厢里堆满板条箱。

branches.en: a truck waiting at the warehouse gate
branches.cn: 等在仓库门口的卡车

branches.en: a coal wagon standing on the sidings
branches.cn: 停在侧线的煤车

branches.en: an old print of a flat cart by the dock
branches.cn: 旧版画里停在码头的平板车

branches.en: a modern truck that still keeps the flat bed of the old wagon

senses.title: No longer having something
senses.definition: the fact or experience of no longer having something that one had
senses.definitionCN: 不再拥有曾经拥有之物的这一事实或经历
senses.example: The loss of the old workshop hit the village harder than anyone expected.
senses.exampleCN: 老作坊的失去对村庄的打击比任何人预想的都重。
senses.why: The word names the state left behind when a possession or condition is no longer there.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指某物或某种状态不在之后留下的那个空缺状态。

senses.title: A person or thing that is missed
senses.titleCN: 被怀念、被惋惜的人或物
senses.definition: a person or thing whose absence is felt as a deprivation by a group
senses.definitionCN: 其缺席被群体感受为缺失的人或物
senses.example: The retired teacher was a great loss to the school.
senses.exampleCN: 这位退休教师对学校是一大损失。
senses.why: Instead of the event of losing, the word can name the thing whose absence is felt.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以不指「失去」这件事，而指那个缺席被感受到的人或物。

senses.title: Money lost in business
senses.definition: the amount by which spending exceeds income in a business or year
senses.definitionCN: 企业或年度中支出超过收入的金额
senses.example: The airline reported a loss for the third year running.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司连续第三年报告亏损。
senses.why: Accounting reverses the idea of gain: what should have come back did not, and the shortfall is the loss.
senses.whyCN: 会计把收益的观念反过来：本该回来的没有回来，缺掉的那部分就是亏损。

senses.title: The death of someone close
senses.definition: the death of a relative or friend, experienced as bereavement
senses.definitionCN: 亲属或朋友的死亡，被视为丧亲之痛
senses.example: She took a long leave after the loss of her father.
senses.exampleCN: 父亲去世后，她请了很长的假。
senses.why: Death is the most absolute form of no longer having someone, so the word serves as its ordinary, gentle name.
senses.whyCN: 死亡是「不再拥有某人」最绝对的形式，因此这个词成了它平常而温和的说法。

senses.title: A decrease in amount or intensity
senses.definition: a reduction in quantity, energy or intensity as something escapes or fades
senses.definitionCN: 随着某物逸出或衰减，数量、能量或强度上的减少
senses.example: Insulation cut heat loss through the walls.
senses.exampleCN: 保温层减少了穿过墙壁的热量散失。
senses.why: Physics treats escaping heat as something that leaves the system, which is a loss to the system.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把逸出的热视为离开系统的某物，对系统而言就是损失。

senses.title: Failure to win a contest
senses.definition: a defeat in a game, election or contest
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、选举或竞争中落败
senses.example: It was their third loss of the season.
senses.exampleCN: 这是他们本赛季的第三场失利。
senses.why: A defeat is the loss of a winning position, and sport shortened the phrase to the single word.
senses.whyCN: 失败就是失去获胜的位置，体育语境把这个短语缩短成一个词。

senses.title: An insured event or sum
senses.titleCN: 保险中的损失事件或金额
senses.definition: the damage or sum that an insurer agrees to cover under a policy
senses.definitionCN: 承保人依保单同意赔付的损害或金额
senses.example: The policy covered the loss of the cargo at sea.
senses.exampleCN: 保单承保了海上货物的损失。
senses.why: Insurance exists to price misfortune, so the word becomes a technical term for the event and its cost.
senses.whyCN: 保险的存在就是为不幸定价，因此这个词成了指事件及其代价的技术用语。

senses.title: The gap left by something valuable
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：珍贵之物消失后留下的空缺
senses.definition: the emptiness or deficit that remains after something valuable disappears
senses.definitionCN: 珍贵之物消失之后留下的空虚或欠缺
senses.example: The loss of trust was harder to repair than the loss of money.
senses.exampleCN: 信任的丧失比金钱的损失更难修补。
senses.why: Generalised, the word names any absence that registers as a deficit, whether the thing was money, heat, a person or trust.
senses.whyCN: 一般化之后，这个词指任何被感受为欠缺的缺席，无论所失之物是金钱、热量、人还是信任。

intro.en: Loss comes from Old English los 'loss, destruction', from a Germanic stem also seen in the verb lose; it has no Latin cognate. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: loss 来自古英语 los「丧失、毁灭」，其日耳曼语词干也见于动词 lose；这个词没有拉丁同族词。年代为约数。

items.en: The noun goes back to a Germanic form meaning 'breaking up, loss', related to Old Norse los 'the breaking up of an army'.
items.cn: 这个名词可追溯到日耳曼语中表示「瓦解、丧失」的形式，与古诺尔斯语 los「军队溃散」相关。

items.en: Old English los meant 'loss, destruction, ruin', and the related verb losian meant 'to be lost, perish'.
items.cn: 古英语 los 意为「丧失、毁灭、毁坏」，相关动词 losian 意为「失踪、灭亡」。

items.en: In Middle English the noun settled into its modern spelling and the verb separated into lose, so the pair now differ in form and sound.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，名词固定为现代拼写，动词则分立为 lose，于是这对词在形与音上都分开了。

items.en: The commercial sense of a shortfall in the accounts developed in the sixteenth century alongside double-entry bookkeeping.
items.cn: 账目中出现缺口的商业义在十六世纪随复式记账一同发展。

items.en: Insurance made the word a term for a covered event, and sport made it a count of defeats; both usages spread in the modern period.
items.cn: 保险使这个词成为「承保事件」的术语，体育使它成为失败次数的计量；两种用法都在近代普及。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed, and the exact dates of the financial and insurance senses are not established.
items.cn: 来源不确定：更早的印欧词根属重构形式，财务义与保险义的确切年代亦未得到证明。

entries.definition: A person who loses, especially one who fails to win; it names a person, not an amount.

entries.definition: From the same Germanic root meaning 'free, loose', but it means 'not tight' and is not a synonym of loss.
entries.definitionCN: 同出表示「自由、松开」的日耳曼词根，但意为「不紧的」，并非 loss 的同义词。

entries.definition: Harm to a thing that reduces its value or usefulness; loss is the value that is gone.
entries.definitionCN: 对物品造成的损害，降低其价值或用途；loss 指已经失去的价值。

entries.definition: The amount by which something falls short, especially in public accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 某物不足的数额，尤指公共账目中的缺口。

entries.definition: A gradual decrease in amount or quality; it describes a process, while loss can be a single event.
entries.definitionCN: 数量或质量的逐渐下降；描述过程，而 loss 可以是一次事件。

entries.definition: The state of being beaten in a battle, game or election; it is narrower than loss.
entries.definitionCN: 在战斗、比赛或选举中被击败的状态；比 loss 更窄。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one absence: something that was there is no longer, and the word then names the thing missed, the money short, a death, an escaping quantity, a defeat, an insured event and finally any deficit at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个缺席展开：原本在那里的东西不在了；这个词再指被惋惜的对象、账上的缺款、死亡、逸出的量、一场失利、承保事件，最后指任何欠缺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty place in a drawer where something used to be.
core.cn: 核心意象：抽屉里一个原本放着东西的空位。

branches.en: ABSENCE: the event of losing and the thing whose absence is felt are two sides of one empty place.
branches.cn: 缺席：失去的事件与缺席被感受的对象，是同一个空位的两面。

branches.en: ACCOUNTS: the money that should have come back did not, and the gap is counted as a loss.
branches.cn: 账目：本该回来的钱没有回来，这个缺口就被计为亏损。

senses.title: At a high volume of sound
senses.definition: in a way that produces a strong, easily heard sound
senses.definitionCN: 以发出强烈、容易听见的声音的方式
senses.example: She called loudly for help from the balcony.
senses.exampleCN: 她在阳台上大声呼救。
senses.why: Loud comes from an old word for a strong sound, and -ly turns that quality into the way an action is done.
senses.whyCN: loud 来自表示强烈声响的古词，后缀 -ly 把这种性质变成了做动作的方式。

senses.title: With insistence, so as to be heard or noticed
senses.definition: in a forceful and public way, so that an opinion or complaint cannot be ignored
senses.definitionCN: 以有力而公开的方式，使某种意见或抱怨无法被忽视
senses.example: The residents protested loudly against the new road.
senses.exampleCN: 居民们大声抗议这条新路。
senses.why: If a sound is loud, it reaches many ears; the word therefore moves from volume to public pressure.
senses.whyCN: 声音如果响亮，就能传到很多耳朵里；因此这个词从音量转到公开施压。

senses.title: In a showy or garish manner
senses.definition: in a style that is too bright, bold or decorated to be quiet or tasteful
senses.definitionCN: 以过于鲜亮、大胆或繁复装饰、毫不含蓄的风格
senses.example: The room was loudly decorated with gold curtains and red walls.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间用金色窗帘和红色墙面装饰得十分扎眼。
senses.why: A loud colour or pattern, like a loud sound, refuses to stay in the background, so the word extends from hearing to sight.
senses.whyCN: 花哨的颜色或图案就像响亮的声音一样不肯退到背景里，于是这个词从听觉延伸到视觉。

intro.en: Loudly is simply loud plus the adverb suffix -ly; loud itself goes back to an Old English word for a strong sound.
intro.cn: loudly 就是 loud 加上副词后缀 -ly；loud 本身可追溯到古英语中表示强烈声响的词。

items.en: The adjective hlūd meant loud or noisy, and it described both voices and the roar of a crowd.
items.cn: 形容词 hlūd 意为响亮的、喧闹的，既形容人声，也形容人群的轰鸣。

items.en: Its reconstructed ancestor is hlūdaz, a form rebuilt from comparison with related Germanic languages.
items.cn: 其重构祖形为 hlūdaz，这个形式是通过与相关日耳曼语言比较重建出来的。

items.en: Generally the word is traced to a root meaning to hear, which also stands behind Latin words for being renowned.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词可追溯到表示「听见」的词根，拉丁语中表示「有名」的词也出自此处。

items.en: Middle English kept loud, and speakers added -ly to make an adverb of manner.
items.cn: 中古英语保留 loud，说话者加 -ly 构成方式副词。

items.en: Modern English loudly covers high volume, insistent public speech and showy appearance.
items.cn: 现代英语的 loudly 涵盖高音量、公开坚持的表达以及花哨的外观。

normalIntro.en: The word is a transparent build: loud plus -ly. Its hooks therefore come from the root for sound, the suffix, and the way loud spreads from hearing to behaviour.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的构造很透明：loud 加 -ly。记忆钩子因此来自表示声音的词根、后缀，以及 loud 从听觉扩展到行为的方式。

normal.en: Loudly is loud plus -ly, so the meaning is simply in a loud way.
normal.cn: loudly 是 loud 加 -ly，意思就是「以响亮的方式」。

normal.en: The older form hlūd already meant noisy, so the word has been about sound for a long time.
normal.cn: 更早的形式 hlūd 已经表示喧闹，所以这个词长期都与声音有关。

normal.en: Aloud uses the same root but means out loud rather than in a loud way.
normal.cn: aloud 用同一词根，但意思是「出声地」，而不是「大声地」。

normal.en: The comparative is more loudly, not loudlier, because the word already ends in -ly.
normal.cn: 比较级是 more loudly，而不是 loudlier，因为这个词本身已以 -ly 结尾。

normal.en: Loudly can follow protest and complain, where the volume is social pressure rather than decibels.
normal.cn: loudly 可以跟 protest、complain 搭配，此时「响」是社交压力而不是分贝。

abstract.en: A sound that is loud pushes into other people's space, and the adverb carries that same push into protest.
abstract.cn: 响亮的声音会挤进别人的空间，这个副词把同样的推力带进了抗议。

abstract.en: The move from a loud voice to a loud shirt shows that English treats both as things that refuse to be ignored.
abstract.cn: 从响亮的嗓音到花哨的衬衫，说明英语把两者都看成不肯被忽视的东西。

abstract.en: Adding -ly to a quality is like turning a colour into a way of painting: loud becomes the manner of the action.
abstract.cn: 给一种性质加 -ly，就像把颜色变成画法：loud 变成了动作的方式。

examples.en: She called loudly for help from the balcony.
examples.cn: 她在阳台上大声呼救。

examples.en: The choir sang loudly enough to carry through the whole building.
examples.cn: 合唱团唱得足够响，声音传遍了整栋楼。

examples.en: The residents protested loudly against the new road.
examples.cn: 居民们大声抗议这条新路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「劳得利」——干活喊号子，声音越喊越大，记住 loudly 是大声地。

intro.en: Loudly is a clean suffix build, and its items show the adjective, the suffix, the noun made from it, and the spelling traps around the root.

latinIntro.en: The root behind loudly is generally linked to a hear-root, and Latin keeps related words for being heard of, that is, being famous.
